## 6. Risk scoring model (deterministic)

The score is a **transparent, rule-based risk index** — not a trained ML model. The LLM never computes scores;
it calls tools that run this model. No company disruption history was available to train or calibrate on,
so the parameters below are documented expert assumptions, all overridable via configuration
(`ScoringSettings`, `WeatherThresholds`).

### Two signals per hazard
| Signal | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Observed** | Open-Meteo daily history, last 5 full years | What actually happened recently at the hub's coordinates |
| **Baseline** | FEMA National Risk Index, hub's county (0–100 national percentile) | Decades of hazard history; captures rare events (landfalls, tornadoes) that 5 years can miss |

`hazardScore = w_obs × observed + (1 − w_obs) × baseline` — if one signal is missing, the other is used alone.

### Hazards
| Hazard | Observed: disruption day (threshold) | Cap (days/yr → 100) | NRI baseline (mean of available) | w_obs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Winter | 60% snow day (snowfall ≥ 1 cm) + 40% hard freeze (min ≤ −12 °C) | 40 snow / 30 freeze | Winter Weather, Ice Storm, Cold Wave | 0.60 |
| Hurricane | Gust ≥ 90 km/h (tropical-storm force) | 3 | Hurricane | 0.25 |
| Flood | Precipitation ≥ 50 mm | 6 | Riverine Flooding, Coastal Flooding | 0.50 |
| Severe storm | Gust ≥ 75 km/h | 12 | Tornado, Hail, Strong Wind | 0.40 |
| Heat | Max temperature ≥ 38 °C | 45 | Heat Wave | 0.60 |

Observed score = `min(100, daysPerYear / cap × 100)`. `w_obs` is low where daily weather is a weak proxy
(hurricanes, tornadoes/hail) and high where it measures the hazard directly (snow, heat).

### Composite
```
composite = 0.5 × worstHazard + 0.5 × Σ(wᵢ × hazardᵢ) / Σwᵢ
weights: Winter 0.25 · Hurricane 0.20 · Flood 0.20 · Severe storm 0.20 · Heat 0.15
```
The worst-hazard term prevents dilution: a hub that is extreme on one hazard (Miami/hurricanes) is
high-risk even if every other hazard is benign. **Ratings:** Low < 25 ≤ Moderate < 50 ≤ High < 75 ≤ Very High.

### Explainability & confidence
Each `HubRiskScore` carries, per hazard: score, observed and baseline parts, **evidence factors** (e.g.
`snowDaysPerYear = 18.4`, `nriHurricane = 97.2`), normalized weight and **contribution** (contributions sum
exactly to the composite), plus the **top two drivers** and data **notes**.
Confidence: **High** = full weather coverage (≥ 90% of the window) and NRI present; **Medium** = one signal
missing/incomplete; **Low** = neither.

### Components (WeatherRisk.Core)
| Component | Pattern / role |
|---|---|
| `WeatherStatisticsCalculator` | Single-pass aggregation of daily rows → `WeatherSummary` (also answers "% of snow days in Denver last year") |
| `IHazardScorer` + 5 implementations | **Strategy** — one per hazard; adding a hazard = adding a class (Open/Closed) |
| `HazardMath` | Shared normalize/blend/single-metric recipe — keeps the four single-metric scorers ~10 lines each |
| `RiskScoringEngine` | Composite, attribution, drivers, confidence; validates settings and scorer set at construction (fail fast) |
| `HubRanker` | Pure ranking (by composite or hazard, region filter, top N, deterministic tie-breaks) and side-by-side comparison |
| `ScoringSettings`, `WeatherThresholds` | Plain settings objects (Core has no dependency on `Microsoft.Extensions.Options`; the Api binds them) |

### Future calibration
With the company's historical closure/delay records, weights and caps could be fitted (e.g. regression in
ML.NET) so the index predicts real disruption days or cost — the model structure stays the same.

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent — Design & Architecture

> Living document: updated in every task branch. Sections marked *TBD* are filled in by the task noted.

## 1. Problem & scope
A logistics company runs regional distribution hubs across the US. Severe weather shuts hubs down and
costs money; each year a handful of hubs get resilience investment. This system is an AI agent that helps
analysts **rank, compare, and explain hub exposure to weather disruption**, conversationally.

**In scope:** 15 US hubs, four hazard categories (winter, hurricane/wind, flood, heat), historical weather
statistics, a deterministic risk score, an LLM agent that uses that score as tools, chat UI with voice,
evaluation set, monitoring, and (bonus) risk-change alerts.

**Out of scope:** real company hub data, financial loss modelling, forecasting, authentication / multi-tenant.

## 2. System architecture
```
 Browser (static HTML/JS chat + voice)
        │  HTTP/JSON
        ▼
 ┌──────────────────────── WeatherRisk.Api (ASP.NET Core, single process) ────────────────────────┐
 │  Middleware: metrics · rate limiting · ProblemDetails          Swagger UI (/swagger)            │
 │  Endpoints: /api/chat · /api/hubs · /api/scores · /api/system/* · /api/alerts                   │
 │                                                                                                 │
 │  Agent ── LLM provider chain (Groq → Gemini) ── JSON-schema validation                          │
 │    │ tool calls                                                                                 │
 │    ▼                                                                                            │
 │  Core: scoring engine (per-hazard strategies → weighted composite), ranking, comparison         │
 │    │                                                                                            │
 │  Data: repositories (EF Core) ── SQLite file   ·   API clients (resilient HttpClient) + cache   │
 │  Background: score recompute scheduler → change detection → alert notifiers (bonus)             │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │ HTTPS                                   │ HTTPS
        ▼                                         ▼
 Open-Meteo Historical API, FEMA NRI       LLM APIs (Groq / Gemini, OpenAI-compatible)
```
*Component details: TBD (tasks 2–10).*

## 3. Repository structure
```
WeatherRisk.slnx                 Solution (new XML format, opens in Visual Studio 2026)
Directory.Build.props            Shared settings: net10.0, nullable, XML docs (missing docs = build error)
Directory.Packages.props         Central NuGet versions
global.json                      SDK pin + Microsoft Testing Platform runner
src/
  WeatherRisk.Api/               Composition root (ASP.NET Core Minimal API)
    Program.cs                   DI registration + middleware pipeline
    Endpoints/                   Endpoint groups (one static class per resource)
    Contracts/                   Request/response records (never EF entities)
    Observability/               Request metrics middleware + collector, health checks
    RateLimiting/                Rate-limiter configuration
  WeatherRisk.Core/              Domain + scoring logic (no infrastructure dependencies)
  WeatherRisk.Data/              EF Core/SQLite persistence + external API clients
tests/
  WeatherRisk.Api.Tests/         Endpoint tests (WebApplicationFactory) + Api unit tests
  (WeatherRisk.Core.Tests, WeatherRisk.Data.Tests are added with their first code in tasks 3–4)
docs/                            Architecture, plan, session transcript
.claude/skills/                  Engineering standards the AI agent must follow
```
**Dependency rule:** `Api → Core ← Data` (Api also references Data for DI wiring). Core references nothing.

## 4. Data storage
**Choice: SQLite (single file, EF Core).**
- Zero install, runs on a laptop, file can ship with the demo; real SQL with indexes and transactions.
- Data volume is small (15 hubs × a few years of daily aggregates, cached API payloads, score history).
- Swap path: EF Core makes moving to PostgreSQL a provider/connection-string change.

*Schema & ER diagram: TBD (task 4).*

## 5. Data sources
| Source | Used for | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| Open-Meteo Historical Weather API | Daily snowfall, precipitation, wind, temperature per hub | None (free) |
| FEMA National Risk Index | County-level hazard risk (hurricane, riverine/coastal flood, winter weather, heat…) | None (free) |
| Groq (primary) / Gemini (fallback) | LLM for tool routing and explanations | Free-tier API key (user-secrets) |

*Details: TBD (task 5).*

## 6. Risk scoring model (deterministic)
*TBD (task 3).*

## 7. Agent design & structured output
*TBD (task 7).*

## 8. Monitoring, rate limiting & resilience

### Request pipeline (order matters)
```
ExceptionHandler → StatusCodePages (ProblemDetails) → Swagger → Routing → RequestMetrics → RateLimiter → Endpoint
```
Metrics run after routing (so requests are labelled by route template, e.g. `GET /api/hubs/{id}`, keeping
the number of keys bounded) and before the rate limiter (so 429 rejections are counted).

### Request metrics — `GET /api/system/metrics`
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total`, `succeeded`, `clientErrors`, `serverErrors`, `rateLimited` | Outcome counters since startup (429 counted separately from other 4xx — it signals load, not a client bug) |
| `requestsInWindow` | Requests in the last `windowSeconds` (default 60) — load indicator |
| `avgLatencyMs`, `p95LatencyMs`, `maxLatencyMs` | Over the last 512 requests per endpoint — bottleneck indicator |

Provided per endpoint and overall (`ALL`). Unknown `/api` routes are grouped as `(unmatched)`.
- **Implementation:** `RequestMetricsMiddleware` → `RequestMetricsCollector` (singleton) → per-endpoint
  `EndpointStats` = `SlidingWindowCounter` (60 one-second buckets) + `LatencyWindow` (ring buffer).
- **Cost:** fixed memory per endpoint, one short uncontended lock per request, no allocations on record;
  sorting for p95 happens only when metrics are read.
- In-memory by design (resets on restart). ASP.NET Core's built-in `http.server.*` meters also work with
  `dotnet-counters` for deeper inspection.

### Health — `GET /api/system/health`
ASP.NET Core health checks; 200 for Healthy/Degraded, 503 for Unhealthy. Dependency checks are added by
the features that own them (task 5: data sources, task 7: LLM).

### Rate limiting
Built-in ASP.NET Core rate limiter, **sliding window per client IP** (default 120 requests / 60 s,
6 segments) on all `/api` routes **except `/api/system/*`** — health and metrics must stay reachable under
load, which is exactly when they're needed. Rejections: `429` + `Retry-After` + ProblemDetails. Settings in
`appsettings.json` → `RateLimiting`, validated at startup. *(Task 7 adds a stricter policy for `/api/chat`.)*

### Resilience & fallbacks
*TBD (task 5: HTTP retry/timeout/circuit breaker + cache fallback; task 7: LLM provider fallback).*

## 9. Evaluation
*TBD (task 9).*

## 10. Design decisions
| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| C# / .NET 10 instead of Python | Toolchain already installed, owner's strongest language; architecture is language-agnostic. |
| Single ASP.NET Core process | Simplest to run locally and demo; no inter-service networking. |
| Free hosted LLM (Groq) over local model | Laptop has no dedicated GPU; local 7–8B models would be ~30 s per agent turn. |
| One OpenAI-compatible LLM adapter | Groq, Gemini and Ollama all expose it → provider switch is configuration only. |
| Static HTML/JS chat UI | Lightweight, served by the API, browser Web Speech API gives voice for free. |
| SQLite | See §4. |
| Minimal APIs grouped in static endpoint classes | Less ceremony than controllers; each group is one file; handlers are plain methods (unit-testable, XML docs flow into OpenAPI). |
| Built-in OpenAPI (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi`) + Swagger UI | .NET 10's native document generator; Swashbuckle only for the UI. Swagger enabled in all environments so reviewers can test live. |
| In-process metrics instead of Prometheus/Grafana | Zero infrastructure; enough to spot load spikes, failures and slow endpoints. |
| `TimeProvider` injected | Time-dependent code (metric windows, later caching/alerts) is deterministic in tests. |
| Rate limit partitioned by client IP | Simple and fair for a demo; assumes no reverse proxy (would need forwarded headers). |

## 11. Assumptions & uncertainty
*Collected throughout tasks, finalized in task 11.*
- Monitoring data is in-memory and per-process; it resets on restart and isn't shared across instances.
- Rate-limit client identity = remote IP address (no auth, no proxy).

Task 3 is finished on branch `feature/domain-scoring`. **Nothing is committed yet.** It's waiting for your review.

## Results
- **Build:** 0 warnings, 0 errors, including tests and analyzers.
- **Tests:** 103 of 103 pass, 75 of them new in Core.

## What's in it (all in `src/WeatherRisk.Core`, pure logic with no I/O)

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Domain/` | `Hub` (with coordinates and county FIPS code for the data lookups), `Region` (US Census regions), `HazardType` (5 hazards) |
| `Weather/` | `DailyWeather` (a struct, to avoid allocations), `WeatherThresholds` (each default explained), `WeatherStatisticsCalculator` (one pass over the daily rows), `WeatherSummary` (per-year rates, % of days, coverage) |
| `Scoring/` | `IHazardScorer` (Strategy) and `RiskScoringEngine` (composite score, attribution, top drivers, confidence, fails fast on bad config), plus `ScoringSettings`, which holds every tunable number |
| `Scoring/Hazards/` | `WinterScorer`, `HurricaneScorer`, `FloodScorer`, `SevereStormScorer`, `HeatScorer`, plus the shared `HazardMath` |
| `Ranking/` | `HubRanker`: rank by composite or by one hazard, filter by region, top N, deterministic tie-breaks, and side-by-side comparison |

The model is implemented exactly as approved. I checked it against hand-worked examples: the end-to-end golden test gives 65.3, and the arithmetic is written out in the test comments.

**The brief's questions map directly onto this code:**
- *Midwest winter:* `Rank(region: Midwest, hazard: Winter)`, tested.
- *Miami vs Houston:* `Compare([miami, houston], [Hurricane, Flood])` reports the most exposed hub and the spread per hazard, tested.
- *% of snow days in Denver:* `WeatherSummary.PercentOfDays(SnowDays)`, tested.
- *Why is Dallas high:* each hazard's contribution (they add up to the composite score), the top drivers and the evidence factors.

**Tests (`tests/WeatherRisk.Core.Tests`):** threshold boundaries (inclusive at the limit, excluded just below), null handling, golden values for each scorer, missing data, the composite math, attribution summing exactly to the composite, all three confidence levels, ranking and comparison, and validation of bad config.

**Docs:** architecture doc §6 now has the full scoring model, plus new design decisions and assumptions (including that the parameters are uncalibrated). The repo structure and the plan are updated too.

## Decisions worth checking
1. **Missing data never counts as zero risk.** If one signal is missing, the score uses the other, and confidence drops with a note. For an inland hub, missing coastal-flood data is simply skipped rather than averaged in as 0.
2. **`HubRanker` is a static class.** It's a set of pure functions with no state, so an interface would add ceremony with no benefit (our anti-over-engineering rule).
3. **Scores are rounded to 1 decimal inside the model,** so the numbers shown to the analyst add up exactly.

One small housekeeping note: the xUnit template had stripped a trailing newline from `global.json`, and I restored the file so it isn't in the diff.

Say **"approved"** and I'll commit and push.

- Swap path: EF Core makes moving to PostgreSQL a provider/connection-string change.
- File: `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db` (git-ignored). Created and migrated automatically on
  startup; safe to delete — it is a cache plus score history and will be rebuilt.
- **WAL mode** is enabled so the background scorer (task 10) can write while API requests read.

### Schema
Live description (columns, types, keys, indexes, comments): **`GET /api/system/schema`** — generated at
runtime from the EF Core model, so it cannot drift from the code. Every table and column carries a comment
(enforced by a unit test).

```mermaid
erDiagram
    Hubs ||--o{ DailyWeather : "has (cascade)"
    Hubs ||--o| WeatherSync : "has (cascade)"
    Hubs ||--o{ RiskScoreSnapshots : "has (cascade)"
    Hubs }o..o| HazardBaselines : "CountyFips (logical, no FK)"

    Hubs {
        TEXT Id PK "lower-case id, e.g. dallas"
        TEXT Name
        TEXT City
        TEXT State
        TEXT Region "Midwest | South | West | Northeast (indexed)"
        REAL Latitude
        REAL Longitude
        TEXT CountyFips "FEMA NRI lookup key"
    }
    DailyWeather {
        TEXT HubId PK, FK
        TEXT Date PK
        REAL SnowfallCm
        REAL PrecipitationMm
        REAL MaxWindGustKmh
        REAL MaxTemperatureC
        REAL MinTemperatureC
    }
    WeatherSync {
        TEXT HubId PK, FK
        TEXT CoveredFrom
        TEXT CoveredTo
        INTEGER SyncedAt "UTC"
    }
    HazardBaselines {
        TEXT CountyFips PK
        REAL WinterWeather "... 10 NRI hazard scores, 0-100"
        INTEGER FetchedAt "UTC"
    }
    RiskScoreSnapshots {
        INTEGER Id PK "insertion order = chronology"
        TEXT HubId FK "index (HubId, Id)"
        INTEGER ComputedAt "UTC"
        REAL CompositeScore
        TEXT Rating
        TEXT Confidence
        REAL WinterScore "... one column per hazard"
    }
```

| Table | Role | Write pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `Hubs` | Reference data, seeded by the initial migration from `HubCatalog` | Migration only |
| `DailyWeather` | Cache of Open-Meteo daily rows (~1,830 per hub for 5 years) | Atomic range replace (set-based delete + batched insert in one transaction) |
| `WeatherSync` | Cache freshness: period + fetch time per hub | Written in the same transaction as `DailyWeather` |
| `HazardBaselines` | Cache of FEMA NRI scores per county | Upsert |
| `RiskScoreSnapshots` | Append-only score history for trends and change alerts | Batched append |

### Data access design
- **Repository pattern with ports in Core:** `IHubRepository`, `IWeatherRepository`,
  `IHazardBaselineRepository`, `IRiskScoreHistoryRepository` are defined in `WeatherRisk.Core/Abstractions`
  and implemented (internally) in `WeatherRisk.Data` — Core never references EF (Dependency Inversion).
  Small, separate interfaces (Interface Segregation) rather than one generic repository.
- **Entities ≠ domain models:** EF entities live in Data and are mapped to Core records; neither is exposed
  over the API (API contracts are separate records).
- **Performance:** pooled `DbContext`; `AsNoTracking` + projection for reads; composite PK `(HubId, Date)`
  serves the range query; `(HubId, Id)` index serves latest/history; change tracker cleared after bulk writes.
- **Migrations** (EF Core, `dotnet-ef` as a local repo tool) are applied at startup; a unit test fails if the
  model changes without a new migration.

# CLAUDE.md — Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption. C# / .NET 10 backend (ASP.NET Core Minimal API), SQLite, static HTML/JS chat UI with voice,
LLM via OpenAI-compatible API (Groq primary). See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/PLAN.md`.

## Mandatory skills — apply ALL of them to every code change, component, and design decision
| Skill | Path |
|---|---|
| Documentation | `.claude/skills/code-documentation/SKILL.md` |
| Swagger / API & schema docs | `.claude/skills/api-swagger/SKILL.md` |
| SOLID & design patterns (no over-engineering) | `.claude/skills/solid-design-patterns/SKILL.md` |
| Performance | `.claude/skills/performance/SKILL.md` |
| Testing (unit + endpoint) | `.claude/skills/testing/SKILL.md` |
| Observability & resilience | `.claude/skills/observability-resilience/SKILL.md` |

Read the relevant skill files at the start of each task and run through their checklists before
reporting the task as done.

## Git workflow (strict)
- One branch per task from `docs/PLAN.md`, created from an up-to-date `main`. No parallel worktrees.
- When a task is implemented and tests pass: **stop and report** (changed files, summary, test results).
  **Do not commit or push until the user approves.**
- After approval: commit + push the branch. The user opens the PR and merges, then says to continue.
- `git` is not on PATH — use Visual Studio's bundled git:
  `C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Community\Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\TeamFoundation\Team Explorer\Git\cmd\git.exe`

## Living documentation
Every task updates, in the same branch:
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — sections touched by the task (components, schema, decisions, assumptions).
- `README.md` — run instructions for anything new.
- `docs/PLAN.md` — task status.

## Secrets
Never commit or print API keys. LLM keys live in .NET user-secrets or environment variables only.

## Commands
- Build: `dotnet build`
- Test: `dotnet test`
- Run API (serves the chat UI + Swagger): `dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api`
- Run evaluation: `dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Eval`

content.text:
Task 4 is finished on branch `feature/persistence`. **Nothing is committed yet.** It's waiting for your review.

## Results
- **Build:** 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- **Tests:** 147 of 147 pass, 44 of them new. No temporary test databases are left behind.
- **Live run:** the database is created on startup with the 15 hubs seeded. Health shows `database: Healthy`, and `/api/system/schema` describes all 5 tables.

## What's in it

**Core: repository interfaces (`Abstractions/`).** These are the ports Data implements, so Core never references EF:
`IHubRepository`, `IWeatherRepository`, `IHazardBaselineRepository`, `IRiskScoreHistoryRepository`, plus `RiskScoreSnapshot` and `Hub.NormalizeId` (so "Dallas", "dallas" and " DALLAS " are treated as the same hub).

**Data: EF Core with SQLite (`Persistence/`)**

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Hubs` | The 15 hubs (from `Seed/HubCatalog.cs`, each with coordinates and county FIPS code), seeded by the migration |
| `DailyWeather` | Cache of Open-Meteo daily rows; the primary key `(HubId, Date)` also serves the date-range query |
| `WeatherSync` | Which period is cached for each hub and when it was fetched |
| `HazardBaselines` | Cache of FEMA NRI scores, one row per county |
| `RiskScoreSnapshots` | Append-only score history, indexed on `(HubId, Id)` |

- Every table and column has a comment, and a unit test enforces this.
- Weather refresh replaces a date range atomically (one set-based delete plus one batched insert), so a failed refresh never leaves half-written data.
- Pooled `DbContext`, no-tracking projected reads, WAL mode, and migrations applied on startup.

**Api**
- `GET /api/system/schema`: tables, columns, keys, indexes and comments, generated from the EF model, so it can never drift from the code.
- A `database` health check.
- The database file resolves to `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`, which is git-ignored.

**Tests**
- **Data.Tests (new project):** runs against real SQLite in memory with the real migrations applied. It covers the repositories (round-trips, nulls, replace without duplicates, isolation between hubs, foreign-key enforcement, newest-first ordering) and the schema (migrations apply cleanly, **no model change without a migration**, every column commented).
- **Api.Tests:** every test host gets its own temporary database file. New tests cover the schema endpoint, the database health check and path resolution.

**Docs:** architecture doc §4 now has a **Mermaid ER diagram**, a table-by-table role list and the data-access design, plus updated repo structure, decisions and assumptions. The README covers the database, resetting it and migration commands.

## Decisions worth checking
1. **The weather cache stores structured rows, not raw JSON.** That allows SQL range queries and avoids re-parsing.
2. **Baselines are keyed by county,** because FEMA NRI data is county-level.
3. **"Latest snapshot" is decided by the auto-increment id,** which is more reliable than ordering by timestamp in SQLite.
4. **No in-memory hub cache.** Reading 15 rows from SQLite takes under a millisecond, so a cache wouldn't be worth the added complexity.
5. **`dotnet-ef` is a local repo tool** (`dotnet-tools.json`), so nothing is installed globally.

Say **"approved"** and I'll commit and push.

I reviewed all added repository interfaces and their implementations for each database table, the entity framework core use for DB model entities, and DB context.
I approve, you can continue to cmmit and push

content.text:
This is a key finding, and it changes the baseline definition you approved, so I want your OK before coding.

## Finding: FEMA's "Risk Score" can't separate big-city hubs

| County (hub) | Winter risk **score** | Winter **frequency** (events/yr) | Hurricane **score** | Hurricane **frequency** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hennepin (Minneapolis) | — | **16.6** | — | n/a |
| Denver | 91.9 | **13.7** | n/a | n/a |
| Dallas | **98.7** | 4.1 | 73.6 | **0.01** |
| Harris (Houston) | 88.8 | 1.1 | 100 | **0.18** |
| Miami-Dade | 0 | 0 | 99.96 | **0.30** |

The risk **score** puts Dallas *above* Denver for winter, and Miami at 99.5 for cold waves. It measures **expected loss to everything in the county**: population, buildings and social vulnerability. Big metro counties top almost every hazard.

The **annualized frequency** (`_AFREQ`) measures how often the hazard actually hits. It ranks the hubs the way you'd expect and doesn't depend on county size, and that's what matters for *our* facility, whose own exposure is fixed.

## Proposal: base the baseline on frequency, expressed as a national percentile
- **One cached fetch** downloads the 10 frequency fields for **all 3,232 US counties** (2 paged requests, a few hundred KB, refreshed every 30 days).
- Each county's value becomes a **percentile rank among US counties** (0–100). So the baseline stays on the same 0–100 scale, the scoring model and DB schema are unchanged, and there are no arbitrary caps.
- A null frequency means the hazard **doesn't apply** there (no hurricane exposure in Denver, no coastal flooding inland). It stays null, and the existing missing-data logic handles it.
- FEMA renamed "Riverine Flooding" to **"Inland Flooding" (`IFLD`)**. I'll map it, and keep the property name, documented.

## The rest of Task 5, unchanged from the plan
- `OpenMeteoClient` and `FemaNriClient` as typed `HttpClient`s with **Polly resilience** (timeout, jittered retry, circuit breaker).
- A **cache-first data provider:** if the window is cached it's served from SQLite; otherwise it fetches live (15 hubs **in parallel, bounded to 4 at a time**, with DB writes kept sequential because the DbContext isn't thread-safe). If the live call fails, it **falls back to stale cache**, and every result carries a freshness flag (`Fresh`, `Cached`, `Stale` or `Unavailable`).
- **Window:** the last 5 full calendar years (2021–2025), which also covers "Denver last year".
- **Dependency metrics** (calls, failures, fallbacks, latency per external API) are added to `/api/system/metrics`. A **health check** reports Degraded when the last call to an API failed. It doesn't call the external APIs itself, so health stays fast.
- **Tests** use stubbed HTTP only, including failure → fallback paths. Nothing calls the internet.

**Do you approve switching the baseline to frequency percentiles?** I recommend it, because without it the FEMA half of the score barely varies across our hubs.
yes approve all changes, continue

content.thinking: Found the issue: Open-Meteo's per-minute rate limit was causing transient failures when fetching 15 hubs at once, with retries still landing in the same quota minute. I'll fix this by extending retry backoff to cross into the next minute, adding a background cache warm-up on startup (disabled in tests), and correcting the hurricane model to zero out hazards FEMA marks inapplicable and drop the hurricane observed weight to 0 since gust data can't distinguish hurricanes from other storms.

| Source | Used for | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| Open-Meteo Historical Weather API | Daily snowfall, precipitation, wind, temperature per hub | None (free) |
| FEMA National Risk Index | County-level hazard frequency (winter, ice, cold, hurricane, inland/coastal flood, tornado, hail, wind, heat) | None (free) |
| Groq (primary) / Gemini (fallback) | LLM for tool routing and explanations | Free-tier API key (user-secrets) |

### Open-Meteo (`OpenMeteoClient`)
`GET archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive` with `daily=snowfall_sum,precipitation_sum,wind_gusts_10m_max,
temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min&timezone=auto` for the hub's coordinates over the window
(last 5 full calendar years, e.g. 2021–2025). Units are already cm / mm / km/h / °C. One request per hub
(~1,826 rows). Response arrays are validated for alignment; coordinates are formatted culture-invariant.

### FEMA NRI (`FemaNriClient`)
Public ArcGIS feature service `National_Risk_Index_Counties` (NRI release "December 2025" at time of writing).
**Design change found during integration:** NRI's *Risk Index Score* scales with a county's population and
property value, so every large metro county scores ~95–100 on nearly every hazard (Miami-Dade = 99.5 for
*cold wave*) — useless for comparing metro hubs. We therefore use **annualized frequency (`*_AFREQ`)** —
how often the hazard occurs, independent of what is built there — and convert it to a **national percentile
among all 3,232 counties** (mid-rank, per hazard). One paged download (2 × 2,000 rows) serves all hubs and is
cached for 30 days. Null frequency = hazard not applicable to the county (kept null).
FEMA renamed "Riverine Flooding" to **Inland Flooding (`IFLD`)**; it maps to `HazardBaseline.RiverineFlooding`.

### Cache-first provider (`HubDataProvider`, implements Core's `IHubDataProvider`)
```
for each hub: cache covers window and younger than TTL? ── yes ──► Cached (no network)
                                    │ no
                                    ▼
              fetch live (≤ 4 in parallel; DB writes stay sequential — DbContext isn't thread-safe)
                 │ success                        │ failure (after retries / timeout / open circuit)
                 ▼                                ▼
     atomic replace in SQLite → Fresh     old cache? ── yes ──► Stale (+ fallback counted & logged)
                                                    └─ no ───► Unavailable
```
Every result carries its `DataFreshness` and retrieval time, which feeds the confidence/notes shown to users.
A background **warm-up** (`DataWarmupService`) fills the cache at startup so the first question is answered
from SQLite (cold fetch of 15 hubs ≈ 50 s due to Open-Meteo's minute quota; cached ≈ 80 ms).

Observed score = `min(100, daysPerYear / cap × 100)`. `w_obs` is low where daily weather is a weak proxy
(tornadoes/hail) and high where it measures the hazard directly (snow, heat). **Hurricane `w_obs` was
lowered from 0.25 to 0 after validating on real data:** daily ≥ 90 km/h gusts also come from nor'easters
(New York) and downslope winds (Denver), so the proxy ranked New York above Miami. Gust days remain visible
as evidence and are used only if the FEMA baseline is unavailable.

### Dependency metrics — in `GET /api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`
Per external dependency: `calls`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `fallbacksServed`, `avgLatencyMs`, `p95LatencyMs`,
`lastCallSucceeded`, `lastSuccessAt`, `lastFailureAt`, `lastError`.
- **Calls/latency** come from `DependencyMetricsHandler`, the *outermost* handler on each typed `HttpClient`
  (so one logical call includes its retries). It lives in the Api; Data stays free of monitoring code.
- **Fallbacks** are reported by the data layer through Core's `IDependencyMetrics` (implemented by the same
  `DependencyMetricsCollector` singleton) — Dependency Inversion, no Data → Api reference.

### Dependency health — `GET /api/system/health`
`database` (EF Core check) plus one **passive** check per external dependency (`open-meteo`, `fema-nri`):
Healthy when never called or the last call succeeded; **Degraded** when the last call failed (cached data is
served, so the API still works — HTTP 200). Passive = no extra calls to free APIs and instant health responses.

### Resilience & fallbacks
| Layer | Open-Meteo | FEMA NRI |
|---|---|---|
| Attempt timeout | 15 s | 30 s |
| Retries (exponential + jitter, honours `Retry-After`) | 4 (5 → 10 → 20 → 40 s) | 2 (2 → 4 s) |
| Total timeout | 150 s | 90 s |
| Circuit breaker | standard (sampling 60 s) | standard (sampling 120 s) |
| Fallback | stale cached rows → `Stale`; none → `Unavailable` | stale cached baseline → `Stale`; none → `Unavailable` |

Open-Meteo's long backoff exists because its free quota is per minute and a 5-year request counts as many
calls — found when a cold fetch of all 15 hubs got 429s for the last 3. *(Task 7 adds the LLM provider fallback.)*

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.

- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only (task 7)

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens Swagger.

## Configuration
`src/WeatherRisk.Api/appsettings.json`:
| Section | Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings` | `WeatherRisk` | `Data Source=App_Data/weatherrisk.db` | SQLite file (relative paths resolve under the Api project) |
| `Monitoring` | `WindowSeconds` | 60 | Window for "requests in window" metric |
| | `LatencySampleSize` | 512 | Recent requests per endpoint used for avg/p95/max latency |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |

## Testing
```powershell
dotnet test
```
Runs unit tests, repository tests (in-memory SQLite with the real migrations) and endpoint tests (the full
HTTP pipeline in memory with a temporary database) — no network access needed.

| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens Swagger.

## Configuration
`src/WeatherRisk.Api/appsettings.json`:
| Section | Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings` | `WeatherRisk` | `Data Source=App_Data/weatherrisk.db` | SQLite file (relative paths resolve under the Api project) |
| `Monitoring` | `WindowSeconds` | 60 | Window for "requests in window" metric |
| | `LatencySampleSize` | 512 | Recent requests per endpoint used for avg/p95/max latency |
| `HubData` | `LookbackYears` | 5 | Observed-weather window in full calendar years |
| | `WeatherCacheDays` / `BaselineCacheDays` | 30 / 30 | Cache time-to-live before refetching |
| | `MaxConcurrentFetches` | 4 | Parallel Open-Meteo requests during refresh |
| | `WarmUpOnStartup` | true | Fill the cache for all hubs in the background at startup |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |

## Testing
```powershell
dotnet test
```
Runs unit tests, repository tests (in-memory SQLite with the real migrations) and endpoint tests (the full
HTTP pipeline in memory with a temporary database) — no network access needed.

content.text:
I've finished Task 5 on branch `feature/weather-data-sources`, but nothing is committed yet. It includes **two scoring changes I made after testing on real data**, beyond the frequency-percentile switch you approved, so please look at those first.

## Results
- **Build:** 0 warnings, 0 errors. **Tests:** 194 of 194 pass (47 new). No test touches the internet.
- **Real APIs:** all 15 hubs load fresh from Open-Meteo, and FEMA covers all 3,232 counties. The real app's startup warm-up filled the cache in about 20 s. Health shows database, Open-Meteo and FEMA all Healthy.

## ⚠️ Two scoring changes that need your OK
When I scored all 15 hubs on real data, the hurricane numbers were wrong: Denver came out at 33, and New York (84) ranked above Miami (76).
1. **Hurricane observed weight goes from 0.25 to 0.** Daily gusts of 90 km/h or more also come from Denver's downslope winds and New York's nor'easters, so they can't identify hurricanes. The hurricane score now comes from FEMA only. Gust days still appear as evidence, and are used alone if FEMA data is missing.
2. **New "not applicable" rule.** If FEMA rates a hazard as not applicable to a county (e.g. hurricanes in Denver), it scores 0, with a `notApplicable` evidence entry.

After these changes: Miami 99, New Orleans 95, Houston 88; Denver, Minneapolis and Seattle 0. The Core goldens are updated (the end-to-end example went from 65.3 to 73.8), and the full real-data table is in the architecture doc §6.

## Fixed during live testing
3 hubs failed on the first cold fetch because of **Open-Meteo's per-minute quota**: a 5-year request counts as many calls. Open-Meteo now backs off longer (5 → 10 → 20 → 40 s, honouring `Retry-After`). I also added a **background warm-up** at startup so users never wait for that cold fetch.

## What's in it
- **Core:** `IWeatherDataSource`, `IHazardBaselineSource`, `IHubDataProvider` (with freshness: `Fresh`, `Cached`, `Stale` or `Unavailable`), and `IDependencyMetrics`.
- **Data, `External/`:**
  - `OpenMeteoClient`: validates the response arrays and formats coordinates culture-independently.
  - `FemaNriClient`: pages through all counties; `NriPercentileCalculator` turns frequencies into percentiles.
  - `HubDataProvider`: cache-first, fetches in parallel (at most 4 at a time) but writes to the DB sequentially, and falls back to stale cache when a source fails.
  - Both clients use Polly resilience.
- **Api:**
  - `DependencyMetricsHandler` (outermost, so one call includes its retries) and `DependencyMetricsCollector`: a `dependencies` section in `/api/system/metrics`.
  - Passive `DependencyHealthCheck`s that report Degraded but keep serving.
  - `DataWarmupService`.
- **Migration** `BaselineFrequencyPercentiles` (column comments only).
- **Tests:**
  - The HTTP clients against stubbed HTTP (query building, paging, ArcGIS error bodies, misaligned arrays).
  - Percentile math.
  - The provider: cache hit, TTL expiry, a new year moving the window, stale and unavailable fallbacks, the concurrency limit, and cancellation propagating rather than triggering a fallback.
  - The metrics handler, collector and health check.
  - The warm-up service.
  - Two full-pipeline tests in the real host: success → cached, and network down → Degraded.
- **Docs:** data sources in detail (§5), scoring corrections plus the real-data sanity table (§6), resilience and dependency monitoring (§8), decisions and assumptions. The README covers the external data and the new `HubData` config.

Do you approve the two scoring changes? If so, say **"approved"** and I'll commit and push.
yes approved

input.new_string:
### Layers
| Layer | Project | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP / composition | `WeatherRisk.Api` | Endpoints (thin), contracts + mapping, middleware, DI wiring, background services |
| Application | `WeatherRisk.Core/Application` | `HubRiskService` use cases: assess, rank, compare, weather statistics — shared by REST endpoints and (task 7) the LLM agent's tools |
| Domain | `WeatherRisk.Core` | Scoring engine, hazard strategies, ranking, statistics, repository/data-source ports |
| Infrastructure | `WeatherRisk.Data` | SQLite repositories, Open-Meteo/FEMA clients, cache-first provider |

Request flow for `GET /api/hubs/dallas/risk`:
```
HubEndpoints.GetRiskAsync → HubRiskService.AssessAsync
   → IHubRepository (hub) → IHubDataProvider (baseline + weather: cache-first)
   → WeatherStatisticsCalculator (window summary) → RiskScoringEngine (5 IHazardScorer strategies)
   → freshness notes → ContractMapper → JSON (enums as names)
```

### API endpoints
| Method & route | Purpose | Brief question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/hubs?region=` | List hubs | — |
| `GET /api/hubs/{id}` | One hub | — |
| `GET /api/hubs/{id}/risk` | Composite + per-hazard breakdown, contributions, evidence, provenance | "Why is the Dallas hub's risk high?" |
| `GET /api/hubs/{id}/weather?from=&to=` | Disruption-day counts, % of days, per-year, totals (default: last full year) | "What % of days in Denver last year had snowfall?" |
| `GET /api/risk/rankings?region=&hazard=&top=` | Rank by composite or hazard | "Which Midwest hubs are most exposed to winter?" |
| `GET /api/risk/compare?hubs=a,b&hazards=` | Side-by-side rows + full breakdowns | "Compare Miami and Houston for hurricane and flood" |
| `GET /api/risk/model` | Live description of the model (weights, thresholds, bands, assumptions) | "How is the score calculated?" |
| `GET /api/system/health · metrics · schema` | Operations (task 2/4/5) | — |

Errors are RFC 7807 ProblemDetails: unknown hub → 404 (`unknownHubs` extension), invalid enum/date/period/top → 400.
Score history endpoints arrive with the scheduler that records snapshots (task 10).

### Request pipeline (order matters)
```
ExceptionHandler → StatusCodePages (ProblemDetails) → Swagger → Routing → RequestMetrics → RateLimiter → Endpoint
```

### Request pipeline (order matters)
```
Swagger → Routing → RequestMetrics → ExceptionHandler → StatusCodePages (ProblemDetails) → RateLimiter → Endpoint
```
Metrics run after routing (so requests are labelled by route template, e.g. `GET /api/hubs/{id}`, keeping
the number of keys bounded) and *outside* the exception handler and rate limiter, so they record the final
status of everything: handled domain exceptions as 404/400 (not 500), unhandled ones as 500, and 429s.
The route label is captured before the request proceeds because the exception handler clears the endpoint.
Domain exceptions are not logged as errors (`SuppressDiagnosticsCallback`) — they are expected outcomes.

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.

- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only (task 7)

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

### External data
On startup the app downloads 5 years of daily weather (Open-Meteo) and FEMA hazard baselines for all hubs in
the background (~1 minute the first time — Open-Meteo's free per-minute quota; then cached for 30 days).
Internet access is needed for that first fetch; afterwards the app works from the cache. Progress and outcome:
`/api/system/health` and `/api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens Swagger.

## Configuration
`src/WeatherRisk.Api/appsettings.json`:
| Section | Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings` | `WeatherRisk` | `Data Source=App_Data/weatherrisk.db` | SQLite file (relative paths resolve under the Api project) |
| `Monitoring` | `WindowSeconds` | 60 | Window for "requests in window" metric |
| | `LatencySampleSize` | 512 | Recent requests per endpoint used for avg/p95/max latency |
| `HubData` | `LookbackYears` | 5 | Observed-weather window in full calendar years |
| | `WeatherCacheDays` / `BaselineCacheDays` | 30 / 30 | Cache time-to-live before refetching |
| | `MaxConcurrentFetches` | 4 | Parallel Open-Meteo requests during refresh |
| | `WarmUpOnStartup` | true | Fill the cache for all hubs in the background at startup |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |

## Testing
```powershell
dotnet test
```
Runs unit tests, repository tests (in-memory SQLite with the real migrations) and endpoint tests (the full
HTTP pipeline in memory with a temporary database) — no network access needed.

content.text:
I've finished Task 6 on branch `feature/hub-risk-api`, but nothing is committed yet. Build: 0 warnings. **Tests: 239 of 239 pass** (45 new).

## Results on real data (live app, current cache)
| Brief question | Endpoint | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Midwest winter | `/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter` | Minneapolis 70.8 > Chicago 56.9 > Detroit 54.1 > Kansas City 43.8 > Indianapolis 40 |
| Miami vs Houston | `/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood` | Hurricane: Miami (98.6 vs 87.6). Flood: Houston (81.4 vs 56.4) |
| Denver snow last year | `/api/hubs/denver/weather` | 17 of 365 days = **4.66%** (2025) |
| Why Dallas is High | `/api/hubs/dallas/risk` | 64.6 High. Flood is the worst hazard (FEMA 97.8th percentile, 47 of 64.6 points), then severe storms (tornado and hail around the 96th–97th percentile) |

A warm request takes about 10 ms.

## What's in it
- **Core, `Application/`:** `HubRiskService` handles the use cases (assess, rank, compare, weather statistics). It's the same service the LLM agent will call in Task 7. It loads only the hubs it needs (region filter), adds stale-data notes, and validates input (comparisons need 2–15 distinct hubs, and statistics periods must fall inside the data window). There are also two domain exceptions: `HubNotFoundException` and `RequestValidationException`.
- **Api:**
  - Thin endpoints in `HubEndpoints` and `RiskEndpoints`, each with Swagger summaries, descriptions that name the question they answer, and all response codes.
  - Contracts per area plus a `ContractMapper`; enums are serialised as names ("Winter", "High").
  - `/api/risk/model` describes the scoring model live from its actual settings.
  - A single `DomainExceptionHandler` turns domain errors into 404/400 ProblemDetails, and they aren't logged as server errors.

## Bugs found and fixed during this task
1. **Scoring config overrides were ignored** for any configuration added after `Program` registers services; a test caught it. Fixed by switching to the options pattern with a validator, so a bad config now fails startup with a clear message (also tested).
2. **Metrics recorded domain 404s as 500** because metrics sat inside the exception handler. The pipeline now runs routing → metrics → exception handler → status-code pages → rate limiter, and the route label is captured early (tested).
3. EF Core SQL logging was flooding the output, so I set it to Warning.

## Decisions worth checking
- **Score history endpoints moved to Task 10,** which is where snapshots get recorded; until then they would always return empty lists.
- **No result cache** on top of scoring, since a warm assessment takes about 10 ms.

Say **"approved"** and I'll commit and push.
approved

Branch `feature/llm-agent` is ready, and user-secrets is enabled for the Api project. This task has a few design choices worth agreeing on before I build them.

## Proposed agent design

**1. LLM access: a small OpenAI-compatible HTTP client of our own, rather than an SDK**
- The protocol is plain JSON over HTTP (`/chat/completions`). Owning it means the same resilience and metrics handlers as our data sources, tests against stubbed HTTP, and one client for Groq, Gemini and Ollama. It's about 150 lines that are easy to explain in the interview.
- **Fallback chain:** Groq → Gemini (if a key is configured). If every provider fails, the response is a clear `503`, and all the deterministic endpoints keep working.

**2. Agent loop: tools plus an enforced structured answer**
- The model gets 6 tools that wrap `HubRiskService`: `list_hubs`, `rank_hubs`, `compare_hubs`, `get_hub_risk`, `get_weather_statistics`, `describe_risk_model`.
- **Structured output:** the model *must* finish by calling a `submit_answer` tool (we use `tool_choice: required`). Its JSON schema is **generated from a C# record** (`AgentAnswer`) with `JsonSchemaExporter`, so the schema and the code can't drift apart.
- **Our code enforces the schema:** the answer is parsed strictly (no unknown fields, required fields present, enum values valid). If it's invalid, the error goes back to the model for one retry.
- **Grounding check:** every number the model reports in its findings must appear in a tool result from that turn. Numbers that don't are flagged in the response as unverified. This keeps the LLM from inventing scores.
- **Answer shape:** `answer` (markdown), `intent`, `findings[]` (hub, metric, value, unit), `keyFactors[]`, `assumptions[]`, `uncertainty`, `followUpQuestions[]`. Our code adds the tool-call trace, data freshness, the provider used and the timing.

**3. Conversation memory: in-memory, behind an interface**
- The last 6 question-and-answer pairs per conversation, expiring after 1 hour of inactivity, with a size cap. Only Q&A text is stored, not raw tool data, to keep prompts small and fast. Swapping in SQLite or Redis later means one new class.

**4. `POST /api/chat`** with a stricter rate limit (10/min per client) and a 60 s overall deadline.

## 7. Agent design & structured output

**Division of labour:** the LLM decides *what to look up* and *how to explain it*; every number comes from
deterministic tools; our code validates the answer before it reaches the analyst.

```
POST /api/chat {message, conversationId?}
  └─ ChatAgent (Core/Agent) ── bounded loop (≤ 8 steps, 60 s deadline) ─────────────────────────────┐
       [system prompt + last 6 Q&A + question] → ILlmClient (tool_choice = required)               │
          ├─ tool calls → IAgentTool (6 tools over HubRiskService) → JSON results back to the LLM  │
          └─ submit_answer(args) → AnswerValidator: 1) strict schema parse  2) grounding check ────┘
  ← ChatResponse: answer, intent, findings[verified], keyFactors, assumptions, uncertainty,
                  followUpQuestions, verification, toolCalls trace, llm {provider, model, steps, tokens, ms}
```

### Tools (`Core/Agent/Tools`)
| Tool | Wraps | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `list_hubs(region?)` | `GetHubsAsync` | Resolve names to ids |
| `rank_hubs(region?, hazard?, top?)` | `RankAsync` | "Which hubs are most exposed…" |
| `compare_hubs(hubIds[], hazards?)` | `CompareAsync` (+ compact evidence for compared hazards) | "Compare Miami and Houston…" |
| `get_hub_risk(hubId)` | `AssessAsync` (full breakdown + evidence) | "Why is Dallas high?" |
| `get_weather_statistics(hubId, from?, to?)` | `GetWeatherStatisticsAsync` | "% of days with snowfall…" |
| `describe_risk_model()` | `RiskModelDescriber` | Methodology |

`AgentTool<TArgs>` (Template Method) generates each tool's JSON schema from its argument record, parses
arguments strictly, and turns domain errors (unknown hub, period outside window) into `{"error": …}` messages
so the model can self-correct instead of failing the conversation.

### Structured output — how the JSON schema is enforced
1. **Single source of truth:** `AgentAnswer` (C# record) → `JsonSchemaExporter` → schema of the
   `submit_answer` tool (all fields required, `additionalProperties: false`, enum values, descriptions).
2. **Forced:** every request uses `tool_choice: "required"`, so the model must end with a tool call; prose
   replies get a reminder.
3. **Validated by our code:** strict `System.Text.Json` options (`UnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow`,
   `RespectRequiredConstructorParameters`, `RespectNullableAnnotations`, no numeric enums) + semantic limits
   (non-empty answer/uncertainty, ≤ 3 follow-ups). Violations are sent back to the model (≤ 2 repairs).
4. **Grounding check:** every number in `findings` must appear in a tool result from this turn (±0.05 or
   integer rounding) and every hub must have been returned by a tool. Unsupported findings are returned with
   `verified: false` and a note — the LLM can't pass off invented scores as facts.

### LLM access (`Data/External/Llm`)
- **`OpenAiCompatibleChatClient`** — our own ~150-line client for `POST /chat/completions`; one class serves
  Groq, Gemini's OpenAI endpoint and Ollama. Source-generated JSON (snake_case), key sent per request, never logged.
- **`FallbackLlmClient`** — Chain of Responsibility over (provider × model):
  **Groq gpt-oss-120b → Groq gpt-oss-20b → Groq qwen3.8-27b → Gemini (if keyed)**. Each failure is logged and
  counted as a fallback (`/api/system/metrics`); all failing → `503` with a hint to the deterministic endpoints.
- Per-provider named `HttpClient` with metrics handler + resilience (30 s attempt, 1 quick retry, **no long
  Retry-After waits** — the next model is faster than waiting out a quota).
- Groq's `tool_use_failed` (malformed tool call by the model) is retried once on the same model.

### Findings from live testing (and what was changed)
| Observation | Change |
|---|---|
| gpt-oss with `reasoning_effort: low` called a non-existent tool `json` instead of `submit_answer` (0/3 in a probe) | `medium` (3/3); prompt names the tool explicitly; same-model retry on `tool_use_failed` |
| Groq free tier: 8,000 tokens/min **per model**; a question costs ~4–6k → bursts got 429 | Three Groq models in the chain (separate quotas); `max_tokens` 2048→1500 (counted against quota); chat rate limit 10/min |
| Comparisons explained differences with invented geography ("low-lying area") | `compare_hubs` returns compact evidence; prompt requires causes from evidence fields |
| Malformed chat body returned 500 in Development | `BadHttpRequestException` → 400 ProblemDetails |

### Conversation memory
`IConversationStore` (Core) → `InMemoryConversationStore` (Api): last 10 turns per conversation, 60 min idle
expiry, max 1,000 conversations (own size-limited `MemoryCache`). Only Q&A text is kept — tool data is
re-fetched cheaply — which keeps prompts small. Swap for SQLite/Redis to survive restarts or scale out.

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.

- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only (task 7)

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood | Miami vs Houston, hurricane and flood |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/denver/weather | Denver last full year: snow days, % of days, … |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/dallas/risk | Dallas risk breakdown: drivers, contributions, evidence |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/model | How scores are computed |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

### External data
On startup the app downloads 5 years of daily weather (Open-Meteo) and FEMA hazard baselines for all hubs in
the background (~1 minute the first time — Open-Meteo's free per-minute quota; then cached for 30 days).
Internet access is needed for that first fetch; afterwards the app works from the cache. Progress and outcome:
`/api/system/health` and `/api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens Swagger.

## Configuration
`src/WeatherRisk.Api/appsettings.json`:
| Section | Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings` | `WeatherRisk` | `Data Source=App_Data/weatherrisk.db` | SQLite file (relative paths resolve under the Api project) |
| `Monitoring` | `WindowSeconds` | 60 | Window for "requests in window" metric |
| | `LatencySampleSize` | 512 | Recent requests per endpoint used for avg/p95/max latency |
| `HubData` | `LookbackYears` | 5 | Observed-weather window in full calendar years |
| | `WeatherCacheDays` / `BaselineCacheDays` | 30 / 30 | Cache time-to-live before refetching |
| | `MaxConcurrentFetches` | 4 | Parallel Open-Meteo requests during refresh |
| | `WarmUpOnStartup` | true | Fill the cache for all hubs in the background at startup |
| `Scoring` *(optional)* | e.g. `WorstHazardBlend`, `Heat:CompositeWeight`, `Winter:SnowDaysPerYearCap` | see `/api/risk/model` | Override any risk-model parameter; validated at startup |
| `WeatherThresholds` *(optional)* | e.g. `SnowDayCm`, `HeavyRainMm`, `ExtremeHeatC` | 1 / 50 / 38 | Disruption-day thresholds |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |

## Testing
```powershell
dotnet test
```
Runs unit tests, repository tests (in-memory SQLite with the real migrations) and endpoint tests (the full
HTTP pipeline in memory with a temporary database) — no network access needed.

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.

- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only

## LLM setup (once)
Store the key in .NET user-secrets (kept in your user profile, **outside the repo**; loaded in Development):
```powershell
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Groq:ApiKey" "<your-groq-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
# Optional extra fallback provider (free key at https://aistudio.google.com):
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Gemini:ApiKey" "<your-gemini-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
```
Outside Development use environment variables instead, e.g. `Llm__Providers__Groq__ApiKey`.
Without any key the app still runs; only `/api/chat` returns 503.

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood | Miami vs Houston, hurricane and flood |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/denver/weather | Denver last full year: snow days, % of days, … |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/dallas/risk | Dallas risk breakdown: drivers, contributions, evidence |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/model | How scores are computed |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Ask the agent
In Swagger (`POST /api/chat`) or from PowerShell:
```powershell
$r = Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body '{"message":"Why is the Dallas hub''s weather disruption risk high?"}'
$r.answer; $r.findings; $r.toolCalls
# Follow-up in the same conversation:
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body (@{ message = "How does it compare with Houston?"; conversationId = $r.conversationId } | ConvertTo-Json)
```

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

### External data
On startup the app downloads 5 years of daily weather (Open-Meteo) and FEMA hazard baselines for all hubs in
the background (~1 minute the first time — Open-Meteo's free per-minute quota; then cached for 30 days).
Internet access is needed for that first fetch; afterwards the app works from the cache. Progress and outcome:
`/api/system/health` and `/api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`.

```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

content.text:
I've finished Task 7 on branch `feature/llm-agent`, but nothing is committed yet. Build: 0 warnings. **Tests: 315 of 315 pass** (76 new). **Secret scan: no API keys anywhere in the changes**, since the key stays in your user-secrets.

## Live results against real Groq
| Question | Model / time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Why is Dallas High? | gpt-oss-120b, 4.3 s | Flood 78.9 (47.3 points), driven by 3.6 heavy-rain days a year and the 97.8th FEMA percentile; then severe storms and heat |
| Follow-up: "…compared with Houston?" | used the conversation memory | Houston's lead comes from hurricanes (87.6 vs 34.3); Dallas leads on severe storms and heat |
| Miami vs Houston | gpt-oss-120b, 4.1 s | Explained only with evidence: FEMA percentiles and heavy-rain days a year. All 6 numbers verified |
| Denver snow last year | 4.3 s | 4.66% of days in 2025 |
| "Capital of France?" | 2.0 s, no tools | Politely out of scope |

## What's in it
- **Core, `Agent/`:**
  - The `ChatAgent` loop, capped at 8 steps and 60 s.
  - 6 tools on `AgentTool<TArgs>`, a template base class that generates each tool's schema and parses its arguments strictly.
  - The `AgentAnswer` contract, `AnswerValidator` (strict schema check plus the grounding check) and the system prompt.
- **Data, `External/Llm/`:** our own OpenAI-compatible client, plus `FallbackLlmClient` with the chain **gpt-oss-120b → gpt-oss-20b → qwen3.8-27b → Gemini** (Gemini only once you add a key).
- **Api:**
  - `POST /api/chat` with its own rate limit (10/min).
  - The in-memory conversation store.
  - 502/503 errors that point to the endpoints that still work without the LLM.
  - LLM health checks and metrics.
- **Refactor:** `RiskModelDescriber` moved to Core, so the REST endpoint and the agent tool share it.

## Problems found during live testing, all fixed and documented in the architecture doc §7
1. **`reasoning_effort: low` made gpt-oss call a non-existent tool `json`.** That was my configuration choice. A probe showed 0 of 3 correct with `low` and 3 of 3 with `medium`, so it's now `medium`, with a same-model retry on `tool_use_failed`.
2. **Groq's free quota is 8k tokens per minute per model,** so bursts of questions hit 429s. I added a third model to the chain and lowered `max_tokens`. A burst of 4 questions was then fully absorbed.
3. **Invented geography in comparisons.** The comparison tool now returns evidence, and the prompt requires causes to come from evidence fields.
4. **A malformed chat body returned 500;** it now returns **400**. Cancellation also now stops the fallback chain immediately.

## Known limitations (stated in the docs)
- The grounding check verifies cited *numbers*, not every sentence of prose.
- The fallback model `gpt-oss-20b` sometimes repeats follow-ups inside the answer text.
- Conversations are lost when the app restarts.

**Optional:** a free Gemini key (from aistudio.google.com) would add a fallback provider with its own quota. That would make a live demo more robust. The command is in the README.

Say **"approved"** and I'll commit and push.
approved

input.new_string:
## 7b. Chat UI (`src/WeatherRisk.Api/wwwroot`)

A static page served by the API at `/` — **no framework, no build step, no CDN** (works offline in a demo).

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Layout: header (health badge, read-aloud, new chat, API link), log, example questions, composer with 🎤 |
| `js/app.js` | Controller: `POST /api/chat`, renders the structured answer, conversation id, health polling, `?q=` deep link |
| `js/markdown.js` | Safe Markdown → HTML (**escape everything first**, then add our own tags) — model output can't inject markup |
| `js/format.js` | Pure helpers (numbers, durations, health colours, ProblemDetails → message) |
| `js/voice.js` | Voice input (Web Speech API recognition) and read-aloud (speech synthesis); hidden if unsupported |
| `css/app.css` | Styling with light/dark themes |

Each answer shows: Markdown text · **"Numbers cited" table with ✓ verified / ⚠ unverified** (the grounding
check) · key factors · confidence & caveats · assumptions · clickable follow-ups · a collapsible
**"How I got this"** panel (tool calls with arguments and timings, model, steps, tokens, duration).
Errors (429/502/503) render as friendly messages, including the hint to the deterministic endpoints.

**Security:** strict Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'self'`, no inline script/style), `nosniff`,
`no-referrer`; assets use `Cache-Control: no-cache` + ETag (not fingerprinted, so browsers revalidate).
Static files short-circuit before routing, so they don't touch API metrics or rate limits.

![Chat UI — answer](images/chat-answer.png)

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.

- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only

## LLM setup (once)
Store the key in .NET user-secrets (kept in your user profile, **outside the repo**; loaded in Development):
```powershell
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Groq:ApiKey" "<your-groq-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
# Optional extra fallback provider (free key at https://aistudio.google.com):
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Gemini:ApiKey" "<your-gemini-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
```
Outside Development use environment variables instead, e.g. `Llm__Providers__Groq__ApiKey`.
Without any key the app still runs; only `/api/chat` returns 503.

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood | Miami vs Houston, hurricane and flood |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/denver/weather | Denver last full year: snow days, % of days, … |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/dallas/risk | Dallas risk breakdown: drivers, contributions, evidence |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/model | How scores are computed |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Ask the agent
In Swagger (`POST /api/chat`) or from PowerShell:
```powershell
$r = Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body '{"message":"Why is the Dallas hub''s weather disruption risk high?"}'
$r.answer; $r.findings; $r.toolCalls
# Follow-up in the same conversation:
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body (@{ message = "How does it compare with Houston?"; conversationId = $r.conversationId } | ConvertTo-Json)
```

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

### External data
On startup the app downloads 5 years of daily weather (Open-Meteo) and FEMA hazard baselines for all hubs in
the background (~1 minute the first time — Open-Meteo's free per-minute quota; then cached for 30 days).
Internet access is needed for that first fetch; afterwards the app works from the cache. Progress and outcome:
`/api/system/health` and `/api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens Swagger.

## Configuration
`src/WeatherRisk.Api/appsettings.json`:
| Section | Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings` | `WeatherRisk` | `Data Source=App_Data/weatherrisk.db` | SQLite file (relative paths resolve under the Api project) |
| `Monitoring` | `WindowSeconds` | 60 | Window for "requests in window" metric |
| | `LatencySampleSize` | 512 | Recent requests per endpoint used for avg/p95/max latency |
| `HubData` | `LookbackYears` | 5 | Observed-weather window in full calendar years |
| | `WeatherCacheDays` / `BaselineCacheDays` | 30 / 30 | Cache time-to-live before refetching |
| | `MaxConcurrentFetches` | 4 | Parallel Open-Meteo requests during refresh |
| | `WarmUpOnStartup` | true | Fill the cache for all hubs in the background at startup |
| `Scoring` *(optional)* | e.g. `WorstHazardBlend`, `Heat:CompositeWeight`, `Winter:SnowDaysPerYearCap` | see `/api/risk/model` | Override any risk-model parameter; validated at startup |
| `WeatherThresholds` *(optional)* | e.g. `SnowDayCm`, `HeavyRainMm`, `ExtremeHeatC` | 1 / 50 / 38 | Disruption-day thresholds |
| `Llm` | `ProviderOrder`, `Providers:{name}:BaseUrl / Models / ReasoningEffort / MaxTokens` | Groq (gpt-oss-120b → gpt-oss-20b → qwen3.8-27b), Gemini | LLM fallback chain; keys via user-secrets |
| `Agent` | `MaxSteps` / `HistoryTurns` / `TimeoutSeconds` / `MaxMessageLength` | 8 / 6 / 60 / 2000 | Agent loop limits |
| `Conversations` | `MaxConversations` / `MaxTurns` / `IdleMinutes` | 1000 / 10 / 60 | In-memory conversation memory |
| `RateLimiting:Chat` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` | 10 / 60 | Per-client limit for `/api/chat` |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |

## Testing
```powershell
dotnet test
```
Runs unit tests, repository tests (in-memory SQLite with the real migrations) and endpoint tests (the full
HTTP pipeline in memory with a temporary database) — no network access needed.
