# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.

- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only

## LLM setup (once)
Store the key in .NET user-secrets (kept in your user profile, **outside the repo**; loaded in Development):
```powershell
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Groq:ApiKey" "<your-groq-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
# Optional extra fallback provider (free key at https://aistudio.google.com):
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Gemini:ApiKey" "<your-gemini-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
```
Outside Development use environment variables instead, e.g. `Llm__Providers__Groq__ApiKey`.
Without any key the app still runs; only `/api/chat` returns 503.

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| **http://localhost:5050/** | **Chat UI** — ask questions by typing or by voice 🎤 (Chrome/Edge) |
| http://localhost:5050/?q=Why%20is%20the%20Dallas%20hub%27s%20risk%20high%3F | Deep link: asks the question on load |
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood | Miami vs Houston, hurricane and flood |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/denver/weather | Denver last full year: snow days, % of days, … |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/dallas/risk | Dallas risk breakdown: drivers, contributions, evidence |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/model | How scores are computed |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Ask the agent
In Swagger (`POST /api/chat`) or from PowerShell:
```powershell
$r = Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body '{"message":"Why is the Dallas hub''s weather disruption risk high?"}'
$r.answer; $r.findings; $r.toolCalls
# Follow-up in the same conversation:
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body (@{ message = "How does it compare with Houston?"; conversationId = $r.conversationId } | ConvertTo-Json)
```

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

### External data
On startup the app downloads 5 years of daily weather (Open-Meteo) and FEMA hazard baselines for all hubs in
the background (~1 minute the first time — Open-Meteo's free per-minute quota; then cached for 30 days).
Internet access is needed for that first fetch; afterwards the app works from the cache. Progress and outcome:
`/api/system/health` and `/api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens the chat UI.

### Chat UI
![Chat UI](docs/images/chat-answer.png)
- Type a question or tap an example; **🎤** dictates (Chrome/Edge — the browser asks for microphone permission);
  **🔊** reads answers aloud; **New chat** starts a fresh conversation (follow-ups keep context until then).
- Each answer shows the numbers it cites with **✓ verified** against the deterministic tools, key factors,
  caveats, follow-up suggestions, and **How I got this** (tools called, model, timing).

## Configuration
`src/WeatherRisk.Api/appsettings.json`:
| Section | Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings` | `WeatherRisk` | `Data Source=App_Data/weatherrisk.db` | SQLite file (relative paths resolve under the Api project) |
| `Monitoring` | `WindowSeconds` | 60 | Window for "requests in window" metric |
| | `LatencySampleSize` | 512 | Recent requests per endpoint used for avg/p95/max latency |
| `HubData` | `LookbackYears` | 5 | Observed-weather window in full calendar years |
| | `WeatherCacheDays` / `BaselineCacheDays` | 30 / 30 | Cache time-to-live before refetching |
| | `MaxConcurrentFetches` | 4 | Parallel Open-Meteo requests during refresh |
| | `WarmUpOnStartup` | true | Fill the cache for all hubs in the background at startup |
| `Scoring` *(optional)* | e.g. `WorstHazardBlend`, `Heat:CompositeWeight`, `Winter:SnowDaysPerYearCap` | see `/api/risk/model` | Override any risk-model parameter; validated at startup |
| `WeatherThresholds` *(optional)* | e.g. `SnowDayCm`, `HeavyRainMm`, `ExtremeHeatC` | 1 / 50 / 38 | Disruption-day thresholds |
| `Llm` | `ProviderOrder`, `Providers:{name}:BaseUrl / Models / ReasoningEffort / MaxTokens` | Groq (gpt-oss-120b → gpt-oss-20b → qwen3.8-27b), Gemini | LLM fallback chain; keys via user-secrets |
| `Agent` | `MaxSteps` / `HistoryTurns` / `TimeoutSeconds` / `MaxMessageLength` | 8 / 6 / 60 / 2000 | Agent loop limits |
| `Conversations` | `MaxConversations` / `MaxTurns` / `IdleMinutes` | 1000 / 10 / 60 | In-memory conversation memory |
| `RateLimiting:Chat` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` | 10 / 60 | Per-client limit for `/api/chat` |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |

## Testing
```powershell
dotnet test
```
Runs unit tests, repository tests (in-memory SQLite with the real migrations) and endpoint tests (the full
HTTP pipeline in memory with a temporary database) — no network access needed.

AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption. C# / .NET 10 backend (ASP.NET Core Minimal API), SQLite, static HTML/JS chat UI with voice,
LLM via OpenAI-compatible API (Groq primary). See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/PLAN.md`.

Read the relevant skill files at the start of each task and run through their checklists before
reporting the task as done.

- When a task is implemented and tests pass: **stop and report** (changed files, summary, test results).
  **Do not commit or push until the user approves.**
- After approval: commit + push the branch. The user opens the PR and merges, then says to continue.
- `git` is not on PATH — use Visual Studio's bundled git:
  `C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Community\Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\TeamFoundation\Team Explorer\Git\cmd\git.exe`

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — sections touched by the task (components, schema, decisions, assumptions).
- `README.md` — run instructions for anything new.
- `docs/PLAN.md` — task status.

## Secrets
Never commit or print API keys. LLM keys live in .NET user-secrets or environment variables only.

## Commands
- Build: `dotnet build`

name: git-commit-messages-ps51
description: On this machine (Windows PowerShell 5.1 + VS-bundled git), commit messages containing double quotes must go through `git commit -F <file>`
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Write multi-line commit messages to a temp file (`Out-File -Encoding ascii`) and use `git commit -F <file>`; never pass a here-string containing `"` to `git commit -m`.

**Why:** On 2026-10-20 (Task 8, moveoai-task repo) PowerShell 5.1 split a `-m` here-string at embedded double quotes and passed the fragments to git as pathspecs. The commit silently failed, and the chained `git push` still created the remote branch pointing at `main`, with no changes on it.

**How to apply:** For every commit in this repo use the message-file approach, and check `git log --oneline -1` before pushing, so a push never follows a failed commit. Related: [[moveoai-task-workflow]].

## 9. Evaluation

`src/WeatherRisk.Eval` is a **black-box** console runner: it talks to the running API over HTTP/JSON only (no
project references), so it evaluates the system exactly as analysts and the chat UI use it. The suite lives
in `eval-cases.json` (data, not code) and has two layers:

| Layer | What it checks | LLM? |
|---|---|---|
| **Model checks** (9) | Expert expectations about the deterministic model via REST: Minneapolis leads Midwest winter; Miami > Houston on hurricanes; Houston > Miami on floods; Denver snow share plausible; Dallas High; Phoenix leads heat; hurricanes not applicable in Denver; Seattle in the bottom 3; all hubs High confidence | No |
| **Agent cases** (13) | The 4 brief questions + follow-up with pronouns, false premise (Seattle "so high"), out-of-scope, methodology, top-3 prioritization, unknown hub (Boston), single-hazard ranking, not-applicable hazard, explicit date range | Yes |

**Agent check types:** `intent` · `toolCalled` (+ argument subset, arrays as sets) · `noToolCalls` · `grounded`
(all findings verified, minimum count) · `mentionsHubs` · `mentionsTopRanked` · `citesApiValue` ·
`mentionsApiText` · `mentionsText`. **Expected values are resolved from the deterministic API at run time**
(e.g. "the top 3 of `/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter`"), so the suite doesn't go stale when
data refreshes — it tests that the agent faithfully reports what the model says.

Run: `dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Eval` (API must be running) → `eval-results/eval-report.{md,json}`;
`--skip-agent` runs only model checks (no key needed). Exit code 0/1/2 = pass/fail/setup error.

### Results (committed: [`docs/evaluation/eval-report.md`](evaluation/eval-report.md))
| Run | Model checks | Agent cases | Agent checks | Latency avg / p95 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9/9 | 11/13 | 43/45 | 3.2 / 4.9 s | A11 → 503 (all models rate-limited, 12 fallbacks); A9 "missing New Orleans" |
| 2 | 9/9 | 12/13 | 46/47 | 2.9 / 4.5 s | A10 "unknown hub" phrase not matched |
| **3 (final)** | **9/9** | **13/13** | **47/47** | **3.9 / 5.9 s** | 5 fallbacks absorbed by the chain |

What the failures taught us — and which side was fixed:
- **Evaluator bugs (2):** the model writes `New Orleans` (narrow no-break space), `heavy‑rain` and
  `don’t`; text checks now normalize Unicode spaces, dashes and apostrophes. The Boston answer ("we don’t
  have a Boston hub") was correct; the phrase list was too narrow.
- **Agent issue (1):** the fallback model appended *Assumptions / Follow-up questions / Intent* sections to the
  answer text, duplicating structured fields in the UI → deterministic `AnswerCleaner` strips such trailing
  label sections (no extra LLM call).
- **Capacity (1):** 13 questions 12 s apart exceeded the free per-model token quotas → default pacing 20 s.
  Under real human pacing this doesn't occur; under bursts the API degrades to a clear 503 with a hint.

LLM answers are non-deterministic: individual runs can differ (e.g. which model answers after a fallback);
the deterministic layer and grounding checks are stable.

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.

- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only

## LLM setup (once)
Store the key in .NET user-secrets (kept in your user profile, **outside the repo**; loaded in Development):
```powershell
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Groq:ApiKey" "<your-groq-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
# Optional extra fallback provider (free key at https://aistudio.google.com):
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Gemini:ApiKey" "<your-gemini-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
```
Outside Development use environment variables instead, e.g. `Llm__Providers__Groq__ApiKey`.
Without any key the app still runs; only `/api/chat` returns 503.

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| **http://localhost:5050/** | **Chat UI** — ask questions by typing or by voice 🎤 (Chrome/Edge) |
| http://localhost:5050/?q=Why%20is%20the%20Dallas%20hub%27s%20risk%20high%3F | Deep link: asks the question on load |
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood | Miami vs Houston, hurricane and flood |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/denver/weather | Denver last full year: snow days, % of days, … |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/dallas/risk | Dallas risk breakdown: drivers, contributions, evidence |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/model | How scores are computed |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Ask the agent
In Swagger (`POST /api/chat`) or from PowerShell:
```powershell
$r = Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body '{"message":"Why is the Dallas hub''s weather disruption risk high?"}'
$r.answer; $r.findings; $r.toolCalls
# Follow-up in the same conversation:
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body (@{ message = "How does it compare with Houston?"; conversationId = $r.conversationId } | ConvertTo-Json)
```

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

### External data
On startup the app downloads 5 years of daily weather (Open-Meteo) and FEMA hazard baselines for all hubs in
the background (~1 minute the first time — Open-Meteo's free per-minute quota; then cached for 30 days).
Internet access is needed for that first fetch; afterwards the app works from the cache. Progress and outcome:
`/api/system/health` and `/api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens the chat UI.

### Chat UI
![Chat UI](docs/images/chat-answer.png)
- Type a question or tap an example; **🎤** dictates (Chrome/Edge — the browser asks for microphone permission);
  **🔊** reads answers aloud; **New chat** starts a fresh conversation (follow-ups keep context until then).
- Each answer shows the numbers it cites with **✓ verified** against the deterministic tools, key factors,
  caveats, follow-up suggestions, and **How I got this** (tools called, model, timing).

## Configuration
`src/WeatherRisk.Api/appsettings.json`:
| Section | Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings` | `WeatherRisk` | `Data Source=App_Data/weatherrisk.db` | SQLite file (relative paths resolve under the Api project) |
| `Monitoring` | `WindowSeconds` | 60 | Window for "requests in window" metric |
| | `LatencySampleSize` | 512 | Recent requests per endpoint used for avg/p95/max latency |
| `HubData` | `LookbackYears` | 5 | Observed-weather window in full calendar years |
| | `WeatherCacheDays` / `BaselineCacheDays` | 30 / 30 | Cache time-to-live before refetching |
| | `MaxConcurrentFetches` | 4 | Parallel Open-Meteo requests during refresh |
| | `WarmUpOnStartup` | true | Fill the cache for all hubs in the background at startup |
| `Scoring` *(optional)* | e.g. `WorstHazardBlend`, `Heat:CompositeWeight`, `Winter:SnowDaysPerYearCap` | see `/api/risk/model` | Override any risk-model parameter; validated at startup |
| `WeatherThresholds` *(optional)* | e.g. `SnowDayCm`, `HeavyRainMm`, `ExtremeHeatC` | 1 / 50 / 38 | Disruption-day thresholds |
| `Llm` | `ProviderOrder`, `Providers:{name}:BaseUrl / Models / ReasoningEffort / MaxTokens` | Groq (gpt-oss-120b → gpt-oss-20b → qwen3.8-27b), Gemini | LLM fallback chain; keys via user-secrets |
| `Agent` | `MaxSteps` / `HistoryTurns` / `TimeoutSeconds` / `MaxMessageLength` | 8 / 6 / 60 / 2000 | Agent loop limits |
| `Conversations` | `MaxConversations` / `MaxTurns` / `IdleMinutes` | 1000 / 10 / 60 | In-memory conversation memory |
| `RateLimiting:Chat` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` | 10 / 60 | Per-client limit for `/api/chat` |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |

## Testing
```powershell
dotnet test
```
Runs unit tests, repository tests (in-memory SQLite with the real migrations) and endpoint tests (the full
HTTP pipeline in memory with a temporary database) — no network access needed.

UI logic (Markdown renderer incl. XSS safety, formatting helpers) — requires Node.js 22+, no packages:
```powershell
node --test "tests/ui/*.test.mjs"
```

# CLAUDE.md — Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption. C# / .NET 10 backend (ASP.NET Core Minimal API), SQLite, static HTML/JS chat UI with voice,
LLM via OpenAI-compatible API (Groq primary). See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/PLAN.md`.

## Mandatory skills — apply ALL of them to every code change, component, and design decision
| Skill | Path |
|---|---|
| Documentation | `.claude/skills/code-documentation/SKILL.md` |
| Swagger / API & schema docs | `.claude/skills/api-swagger/SKILL.md` |
| SOLID & design patterns (no over-engineering) | `.claude/skills/solid-design-patterns/SKILL.md` |
| Performance | `.claude/skills/performance/SKILL.md` |
| Testing (unit + endpoint) | `.claude/skills/testing/SKILL.md` |
| Observability & resilience | `.claude/skills/observability-resilience/SKILL.md` |

Read the relevant skill files at the start of each task and run through their checklists before
reporting the task as done.

## Git workflow (strict)
- One branch per task from `docs/PLAN.md`, created from an up-to-date `main`. No parallel worktrees.
- When a task is implemented and tests pass: **stop and report** (changed files, summary, test results).
  **Do not commit or push until the user approves.**
- After approval: commit + push the branch. The user opens the PR and merges, then says to continue.
- `git` is not on PATH — use Visual Studio's bundled git:
  `C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Community\Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\TeamFoundation\Team Explorer\Git\cmd\git.exe`

## Living documentation
Every task updates, in the same branch:
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — sections touched by the task (components, schema, decisions, assumptions).
- `README.md` — run instructions for anything new.
- `docs/PLAN.md` — task status.

## Secrets
Never commit or print API keys. LLM keys live in .NET user-secrets or environment variables only.

## Commands
- Build: `dotnet build`
- Test: `dotnet test` (and UI JS: `node --test "tests/ui/*.test.mjs"`)
- Run API (serves the chat UI + Swagger): `dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api`
- Run evaluation: `dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Eval`
- New migration: `dotnet tool restore; dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations`

I've finished Task 9 on branch `feature/evaluation`, but nothing is committed yet. **Tests:** 370 of 370 .NET (46 new) and 15 of 15 UI. The committed report contains no secrets.

## Evaluation results (live, real Groq)
| Run | Model checks | Agent cases | Agent checks | Avg / p95 latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9/9 | 11/13 | 43/45 | 3.2 / 4.9 s |
| 2 | 9/9 | 12/13 | 46/47 | 2.9 / 4.5 s |
| **3 (committed)** | **9/9** | **13/13** | **47/47** | **3.9 / 5.9 s** |

The committed report is at `docs/evaluation/eval-report.md`. It has a per-case table plus every check with expected vs. actual and the full answer text.

## What's in it
- **`src/WeatherRisk.Eval`:** a black-box runner that talks only to the running API over HTTP, with no references to internal code. It produces Markdown and JSON reports and exits 0, 1 or 2 for pass, fail or setup error.
- **`eval-cases.json`:**
  - **9 model checks (no LLM):** expert expectations for the deterministic scores. Minneapolis leads Midwest winter, Miami beats Houston on hurricanes, Houston beats Miami on floods, Denver's hurricane score is 0, Seattle is in the bottom 3, and so on.
  - **13 agent cases:** the brief's 4 questions, a follow-up using pronouns, a **false premise** ("why is Seattle so high?"), an out-of-scope question, a methodology question, top-3 prioritisation, an **unknown hub** (Boston), heat ranking, a not-applicable hazard, and an explicit 2024 date range.
  - **Expected values are resolved from the deterministic API at run time,** so the suite doesn't go stale when data refreshes.
- **Commands:** `dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Eval`, or add `--skip-agent` for model checks only (seconds, no key needed). There are also `--only`, `--delay` and `--base-url`.

## What the failing runs showed (also documented in the architecture doc §9)
- **2 evaluator bugs, not agent problems:** the model writes non-breaking spaces (`New Orleans`), non-breaking hyphens and curly apostrophes (`don’t`), and my text checks didn't normalise them. The "Boston" answer was correct; my phrase list was too narrow.
- **1 real agent issue (fixed):** the fallback model appended Assumptions, Follow-ups and Intent sections to the answer text, so the UI showed them twice. A new deterministic `AnswerCleaner` removes those trailing label sections without an extra LLM call. It's tested, including the cases where it must *not* cut.
- **Capacity:** 12-second pacing exceeded the free per-model quotas (one 503), so the default is now 20 seconds.

I also caught and handled the Task 8 merge problem before starting, so this branch is built on the merged chat UI.

Say **"approved"** and I'll commit and push.

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent — Design & Architecture

> Living document: updated in every task branch. Sections marked *TBD* are filled in by the task noted.

## 1. Problem & scope
A logistics company runs regional distribution hubs across the US. Severe weather shuts hubs down and
costs money; each year a handful of hubs get resilience investment. This system is an AI agent that helps
analysts **rank, compare, and explain hub exposure to weather disruption**, conversationally.

**In scope:** 15 US hubs, four hazard categories (winter, hurricane/wind, flood, heat), historical weather
statistics, a deterministic risk score, an LLM agent that uses that score as tools, chat UI with voice,
evaluation set, monitoring, and (bonus) risk-change alerts.

**Out of scope:** real company hub data, financial loss modelling, forecasting, authentication / multi-tenant.

## 2. System architecture
```
 Browser (static HTML/JS chat + voice)
        │  HTTP/JSON
        ▼
 ┌──────────────────────── WeatherRisk.Api (ASP.NET Core, single process) ────────────────────────┐
 │  Middleware: metrics · rate limiting · ProblemDetails          Swagger UI (/swagger)            │
 │  Endpoints: /api/chat · /api/hubs · /api/scores · /api/system/* · /api/alerts                   │
 │                                                                                                 │
 │  Agent ── LLM provider chain (Groq → Gemini) ── JSON-schema validation                          │
 │    │ tool calls                                                                                 │
 │    ▼                                                                                            │
 │  Core: scoring engine (per-hazard strategies → weighted composite), ranking, comparison         │
 │    │                                                                                            │
 │  Data: repositories (EF Core) ── SQLite file   ·   API clients (resilient HttpClient) + cache   │
 │  Background: score recompute scheduler → change detection → alert notifiers (bonus)             │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │ HTTPS                                   │ HTTPS
        ▼                                         ▼
 Open-Meteo Historical API, FEMA NRI       LLM APIs (Groq / Gemini, OpenAI-compatible)
```
### Layers
| Layer | Project | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP / composition | `WeatherRisk.Api` | Endpoints (thin), contracts + mapping, middleware, DI wiring, background services |
| Application | `WeatherRisk.Core/Application` | `HubRiskService` use cases: assess, rank, compare, weather statistics — shared by REST endpoints and (task 7) the LLM agent's tools |
| Domain | `WeatherRisk.Core` | Scoring engine, hazard strategies, ranking, statistics, repository/data-source ports |
| Infrastructure | `WeatherRisk.Data` | SQLite repositories, Open-Meteo/FEMA clients, cache-first provider |

Request flow for `GET /api/hubs/dallas/risk`:
```
HubEndpoints.GetRiskAsync → HubRiskService.AssessAsync
   → IHubRepository (hub) → IHubDataProvider (baseline + weather: cache-first)
   → WeatherStatisticsCalculator (window summary) → RiskScoringEngine (5 IHazardScorer strategies)
   → freshness notes → ContractMapper → JSON (enums as names)
```

### API endpoints
| Method & route | Purpose | Brief question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/hubs?region=` | List hubs | — |
| `GET /api/hubs/{id}` | One hub | — |
| `GET /api/hubs/{id}/risk` | Composite + per-hazard breakdown, contributions, evidence, provenance | "Why is the Dallas hub's risk high?" |
| `GET /api/hubs/{id}/weather?from=&to=` | Disruption-day counts, % of days, per-year, totals (default: last full year) | "What % of days in Denver last year had snowfall?" |
| `GET /api/risk/rankings?region=&hazard=&top=` | Rank by composite or hazard | "Which Midwest hubs are most exposed to winter?" |
| `GET /api/risk/compare?hubs=a,b&hazards=` | Side-by-side rows + full breakdowns | "Compare Miami and Houston for hurricane and flood" |
| `GET /api/risk/model` | Live description of the model (weights, thresholds, bands, assumptions) | "How is the score calculated?" |
| `POST /api/chat` | Conversational agent (§7): any of the above in natural language, with follow-ups | All of them |
| `GET /api/system/health · metrics · schema` | Operations (task 2/4/5) | — |

Errors are RFC 7807 ProblemDetails: unknown hub → 404 (`unknownHubs` extension), invalid enum/date/period/top → 400.
Score history endpoints arrive with the scheduler that records snapshots (task 10).

## 3. Repository structure
```
WeatherRisk.slnx                 Solution (new XML format, opens in Visual Studio 2026)
Directory.Build.props            Shared settings: net10.0, nullable, XML docs (missing docs = build error)
Directory.Packages.props         Central NuGet versions
global.json                      SDK pin + Microsoft Testing Platform runner
src/
  WeatherRisk.Api/               Composition root (ASP.NET Core Minimal API)
    Program.cs                   DI registration + middleware pipeline
    Endpoints/                   Endpoint groups: System, Hubs, Risk, Chat (one static class per resource)
    Contracts/                   Records per area (System, Hubs, Risk, Chat) + mappers
    Risk/                        Risk-model DI registration
    Agent/                       Agent DI registration, in-memory conversation store
    Errors/                      DomainExceptionHandler (domain exceptions → 404/400 ProblemDetails)
    Observability/               Request + dependency metrics, health checks
    RateLimiting/                Rate-limiter configuration
    Persistence/                 SQLite path resolution, schema describer
    Background/                  Hosted services (data warm-up)
    ChatUi/                      Static UI hosting (default files, security headers)
    wwwroot/                     Chat UI: index.html, css/app.css, js/{app,markdown,format,voice}.js
  WeatherRisk.Core/              Domain + scoring logic (no infrastructure dependencies)
    Domain/                      Hub, Region, HazardType

## 11. Assumptions & uncertainty
*Collected throughout tasks, finalized in task 11.*
- Monitoring data is in-memory and per-process; it resets on restart and isn't shared across instances.
- Rate-limit client identity = remote IP address (no auth, no proxy).
- **Scoring parameters are uncalibrated expert assumptions** (thresholds, caps, weights, 50/50 worst-hazard
  blend). They produce a sensible *relative* ranking but are not a prediction of disruption days or cost.
- Daily max gust is a coarse proxy for tornadoes/hail and hurricanes, hence the heavy NRI weighting there.
- Point weather at hub coordinates stands in for the hub's operating area (roads/suppliers may differ).
- FEMA NRI is county-level; we use hazard *frequency* percentiles (how often, relative to US counties), not
  severity or our facility's vulnerability. Frequency units differ per hazard (events vs event-days per year),
  which percentiles normalize away.
- "Not applicable" in NRI (null frequency) is treated as zero exposure for that hazard.
- Open-Meteo values are reanalysis/model-based estimates at a grid point near the hub, not station readings.
- 5 years of observations is short for rare hazards; the baseline compensates but uncertainty remains.
- Hub locations are city centres of real US cities standing in for the company's (unknown) hub sites.
- **LLM limits:** grounding verifies cited *numbers*, not every sentence — prose can still over-interpret
  (mitigated by prompt rules and evidence-rich tool results). The fallback model (gpt-oss-20b) follows
  formatting rules less strictly (e.g. sometimes repeats follow-ups inside the answer text).
- Groq free tier ≈ 8,000 tokens/min per model ≈ 1–2 questions/min per model; the chain spreads bursts across

## 11. Assumptions & uncertainty

### Assumptions (domain and data)
| Area | Assumption | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Hubs | 15 real US city centres stand in for the company's (unknown) hub sites; includes every city in the brief | Point/county data may differ from the exact facility |
| Model parameters | **Thresholds, caps, weights and the 50/50 worst-hazard blend are uncalibrated expert assumptions** | Scores rank *relative* exposure; they don't predict closure days or cost |
| Observed weather | Open-Meteo reanalysis at a grid point near the hub, last 5 full calendar years | Model estimates, not station readings; 5 years is short for rare hazards |
| FEMA baseline | County *frequency* percentiles vs all US counties (not NRI risk scores, which scale with population/property) | Frequency ≠ severity, and says nothing about our facility's vulnerability |
| Not applicable | NRI null frequency = no exposure (hazard scores 0, e.g. hurricanes in Denver) | Correct for hurricanes/coastal flooding inland; noted in the evidence |
| Proxies | Daily max gust is a weak proxy for tornado/hail and can't identify hurricanes | Hence FEMA dominates those hazards (hurricane observed weight = 0) |
| "Last year" | The last full calendar year in the window (2025 when run in 2026) | Partial current-year data would bias rates |

### How uncertainty is communicated to the analyst
- **Confidence** on every score (High / Medium / Low) from data completeness, plus **notes** when data is
  missing or partial.
- **Data provenance** on every assessment: window, `Fresh / Cached / Stale / Unavailable`, retrieval time —
  stale cache after an outage is served *and flagged*.
- **Evidence and contributions** per hazard, so a score can be traced to its inputs; `/api/risk/model`
  states the model and its assumptions.
- The agent's answer has explicit **`uncertainty`** and **`assumptions`** fields, and every cited number is
  marked **verified / unverified** by the grounding check (shown as ✓ / ⚠ in the UI).
- The agent is instructed to **correct false premises** (eval case A6: "why is Seattle so high?" → it is Low).

### Known limitations
- **LLM:** grounding verifies cited *numbers*, not every sentence — prose can still over-interpret (mitigated
  by prompt rules and evidence-rich tool results). Answers are non-deterministic run to run.
- **Free-tier capacity:** Groq ≈ 8,000 tokens/min per model ≈ 1–2 questions/min per model; the chain spreads
  bursts over three models; beyond that `/api/chat` returns 503 while all deterministic endpoints keep working.
- **State is per process:** conversations, request metrics and the rate limiter are in memory (lost on
  restart, not shared across instances). The SQLite cache and score history persist.
- **No auth:** rate limiting is per client IP and assumes no reverse proxy.

## 12. Requirements traceability

| Assignment requirement | Where / how | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Answer the 4 example questions | Agent tools + REST: rankings (`region=Midwest&hazard=Winter`), compare, weather stats, risk breakdown — eval cases A1–A4 pass | ✅ |
| Use public APIs for weather and hazard data | Open-Meteo Historical (§5), FEMA National Risk Index (§5) — free, no keys | ✅ |
| Rank or compare hubs on a defined KPI | Composite risk index 0–100 + per-hazard scores (§6); `HubRanker` | ✅ |
| Explain reasoning clearly | Drivers, contributions summing to the composite, evidence, notes (§6); agent prompt + `keyFactors` (§7) | ✅ |
| Conversational follow-ups | Conversation memory (§7); eval A5 ("How does *it* compare … on *those drivers*?") passes | ✅ |
| Deterministic scoring, not only LLM output | `RiskScoringEngine` (pure, golden-tested); the LLM never computes scores; grounding check | ✅ |
| Chat interface (voice bonus) | `wwwroot` chat UI (§7b) with 🎤 voice input and 🔊 read-aloud | ✅ + bonus |
| Agent exposed through an API used by the chat UI | `POST /api/chat`; the UI calls only this API | ✅ |
| Structured output (JSON schema) between LLM and code | `submit_answer` schema generated from `AgentAnswer`, forced tool call, strict parse + repair (§7) | ✅ |
| Small evaluation set and a way to run it | `WeatherRisk.Eval` + `eval-cases.json` (§9); 9/9 model checks, 13/13 agent cases | ✅ |
| Communicate assumptions, uncertainty, scoping | §1, §11; confidence/provenance/uncertainty in every response | ✅ |
| Bonus: scheduled/webhook alert on score change | Not built (time); storage ready (`RiskScoreSnapshots`), design in §13 | ⬜ |
| Source code + run instructions | Repository + [README](../README.md) | ✅ |
| Live demo (URL preferred, not mandatory) | Runs locally with one command; not deployed | ✅ local |
| Design doc: architecture, repo structure, data storage | §2, §3, §4 | ✅ |
| Full AI session (plan + conversation) | [session/session-transcript.md](session/session-transcript.md) + raw log; plan in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) | ✅ |

## 13. Future work
- **Risk-change alerts (bonus, designed, not built):** a `BackgroundService` re-scores all hubs on a schedule
  (and after data refreshes), appends `RiskScoreSnapshots` (table and repository already exist), compares each
  hub with its previous snapshot, and on a rating change or a composite move ≥ N points publishes an event to
  `IAlertNotifier` observers (log, webhook with retry); `/api/alerts` and `/api/hubs/{id}/history` expose them.
- **Calibration:** fit weights/caps to the company's closure and cost history (e.g. regression in ML.NET) so the
  index predicts disruption days or cost; keep the same explainable structure.
- **Operations:** deploy (container + managed LLM key), persist conversations (SQLite/Redis implementation of
  `IConversationStore`), authentication and per-user rate limits, OpenTelemetry export of the existing metrics.
- **Data:** company hub coordinates and operating area, forecasts / live NWS alerts for near-term risk.

### Assumptions (domain and data)
| Area | Assumption | Why it matters |

1	# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent
2	
3	An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
4	disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
5	scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.
6	
7	- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
8	- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)
9	
10	## Prerequisites
11	- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
12	- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only
13	
14	## LLM setup (once)
15	Store the key in .NET user-secrets (kept in your user profile, **outside the repo**; loaded in Development):
16	```powershell
17	dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Groq:ApiKey" "<your-groq-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
18	# Optional extra fallback provider (free key at https://aistudio.google.com):
19	dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Gemini:ApiKey" "<your-gemini-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
20	```
21	Outside Development use environment variables instead, e.g. `Llm__Providers__Groq__ApiKey`.
22	Without any key the app still runs; only `/api/chat` returns 503.
23	
24	## Running
25	
26	### Command line
27	```powershell
28	dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
29	```
30	Then open:
31	| URL | What |
32	|---|---|
33	| **http://localhost:5050/** | **Chat UI** — ask questions by typing or by voice 🎤 (Chrome/Edge) |
34	| http://localhost:5050/?q=Why%20is%20the%20Dallas%20hub%27s%20risk%20high%3F | Deep link: asks the question on load |
35	| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
36	| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter |
37	| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood | Miami vs Houston, hurricane and flood |
38	| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/denver/weather | Denver last full year: snow days, % of days, … |
39	| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/dallas/risk | Dallas risk breakdown: drivers, contributions, evidence |
40	| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/model | How scores are computed |
41	| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
42	| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
43	| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
44	| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |
45	
46	### Ask the agent
47	In Swagger (`POST /api/chat`) or from PowerShell:
48	```powershell
49	$r = Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
50	      -Body '{"message":"Why is the Dallas hub''s weather disruption risk high?"}'
51	$r.answer; $r.findings; $r.toolCalls
52	# Follow-up in the same conversation:
53	Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
54	      -Body (@{ message = "How does it compare with Houston?"; conversationId = $r.conversationId } | ConvertTo-Json)
55	```
56	
57	### Database
58	SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
59	(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.
60	
61	### External data

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data, a deterministic
scoring model, and an LLM for conversation.

- **Design & architecture:** [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Task plan:** [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only

## LLM setup (once)
Store the key in .NET user-secrets (kept in your user profile, **outside the repo**; loaded in Development):
```powershell
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Groq:ApiKey" "<your-groq-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
# Optional extra fallback provider (free key at https://aistudio.google.com):
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Gemini:ApiKey" "<your-gemini-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
```
Outside Development use environment variables instead, e.g. `Llm__Providers__Groq__ApiKey`.
Without any key the app still runs; only `/api/chat` returns 503.

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| **http://localhost:5050/** | **Chat UI** — ask questions by typing or by voice 🎤 (Chrome/Edge) |
| http://localhost:5050/?q=Why%20is%20the%20Dallas%20hub%27s%20risk%20high%3F | Deep link: asks the question on load |
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood | Miami vs Houston, hurricane and flood |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/denver/weather | Denver last full year: snow days, % of days, … |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/dallas/risk | Dallas risk breakdown: drivers, contributions, evidence |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/model | How scores are computed |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Ask the agent
In Swagger (`POST /api/chat`) or from PowerShell:
```powershell
$r = Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body '{"message":"Why is the Dallas hub''s weather disruption risk high?"}'
$r.answer; $r.findings; $r.toolCalls
# Follow-up in the same conversation:
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body (@{ message = "How does it compare with Houston?"; conversationId = $r.conversationId } | ConvertTo-Json)
```

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

### External data
On startup the app downloads 5 years of daily weather (Open-Meteo) and FEMA hazard baselines for all hubs in
the background (~1 minute the first time — Open-Meteo's free per-minute quota; then cached for 30 days).
Internet access is needed for that first fetch; afterwards the app works from the cache. Progress and outcome:
`/api/system/health` and `/api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens the chat UI.

### Chat UI
![Chat UI](docs/images/chat-answer.png)
- Type a question or tap an example; **🎤** dictates (Chrome/Edge — the browser asks for microphone permission);
  **🔊** reads answers aloud; **New chat** starts a fresh conversation (follow-ups keep context until then).
- Each answer shows the numbers it cites with **✓ verified** against the deterministic tools, key factors,
  caveats, follow-up suggestions, and **How I got this** (tools called, model, timing).

## Configuration
`src/WeatherRisk.Api/appsettings.json`:
| Section | Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings` | `WeatherRisk` | `Data Source=App_Data/weatherrisk.db` | SQLite file (relative paths resolve under the Api project) |
| `Monitoring` | `WindowSeconds` | 60 | Window for "requests in window" metric |
| | `LatencySampleSize` | 512 | Recent requests per endpoint used for avg/p95/max latency |
| `HubData` | `LookbackYears` | 5 | Observed-weather window in full calendar years |
| | `WeatherCacheDays` / `BaselineCacheDays` | 30 / 30 | Cache time-to-live before refetching |
| | `MaxConcurrentFetches` | 4 | Parallel Open-Meteo requests during refresh |
| | `WarmUpOnStartup` | true | Fill the cache for all hubs in the background at startup |
| `Scoring` *(optional)* | e.g. `WorstHazardBlend`, `Heat:CompositeWeight`, `Winter:SnowDaysPerYearCap` | see `/api/risk/model` | Override any risk-model parameter; validated at startup |
| `WeatherThresholds` *(optional)* | e.g. `SnowDayCm`, `HeavyRainMm`, `ExtremeHeatC` | 1 / 50 / 38 | Disruption-day thresholds |
| `Llm` | `ProviderOrder`, `Providers:{name}:BaseUrl / Models / ReasoningEffort / MaxTokens` | Groq (gpt-oss-120b → gpt-oss-20b → qwen3.8-27b), Gemini | LLM fallback chain; keys via user-secrets |
| `Agent` | `MaxSteps` / `HistoryTurns` / `TimeoutSeconds` / `MaxMessageLength` | 8 / 6 / 60 / 2000 | Agent loop limits |
| `Conversations` | `MaxConversations` / `MaxTurns` / `IdleMinutes` | 1000 / 10 / 60 | In-memory conversation memory |
| `RateLimiting:Chat` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` | 10 / 60 | Per-client limit for `/api/chat` |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |

## Evaluation
With the API running (`dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http`), in a second terminal:
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Eval                  # 9 model checks + 13 agent cases (~6 min, paced for free LLM quotas)
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Eval -- --skip-agent  # model checks only, seconds, no API key needed
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Eval -- --only A1,A4  # selected cases
```
Reports are written to `eval-results/eval-report.md` and `.json`. Cases live in
`src/WeatherRisk.Eval/eval-cases.json`. Latest committed run: [docs/evaluation/eval-report.md](docs/evaluation/eval-report.md)
(**9/9 model checks, 13/13 agent cases, 47/47 checks**). Options: `--base-url`, `--cases`, `--out`, `--delay`.

## Testing
```powershell
dotnet test
```
Runs unit tests, repository tests (in-memory SQLite with the real migrations) and endpoint tests (the full
HTTP pipeline in memory with a temporary database) — no network access needed.

UI logic (Markdown renderer incl. XSS safety, formatting helpers) — requires Node.js 22+, no packages:
```powershell
node --test "tests/ui/*.test.mjs"
```

# Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

An AI agent that helps logistics analysts decide which US distribution hubs are most exposed to weather
disruption — ranking, comparing and explaining hub risk using public weather/hazard data (Open-Meteo,
FEMA National Risk Index), a **deterministic, explainable scoring model**, and an LLM agent that answers in
natural language (with follow-ups and voice) through a JSON-schema-enforced, grounding-checked contract.

## Quick start
```powershell
# 1. One-time: store a free Groq key (https://console.groq.com) outside the repo
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Groq:ApiKey" "<your-groq-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
# 2. Run (creates the SQLite DB and downloads weather/FEMA data in the background on first start, ~1 min)
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
# 3. Open http://localhost:5050  (chat UI)  ·  http://localhost:5050/swagger  (API)
```

## Deliverables
| | |
|---|---|
| Design & architecture (components, repo structure, data storage, decisions, assumptions, requirements traceability) | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) |
| Evaluation set, runner and latest results (9/9 model checks, 13/13 agent cases) | [src/WeatherRisk.Eval](src/WeatherRisk.Eval) · [docs/evaluation/eval-report.md](docs/evaluation/eval-report.md) |
| Full AI session (plan, discussion, every review round) | [docs/session/session-transcript.md](docs/session/session-transcript.md) (+ raw log) |
| Task plan and status | [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) |
| Engineering standards the AI agent followed | [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) · [.claude/skills](.claude/skills) |

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK (`dotnet --list-sdks` should show 10.0.x)
- A free Groq API key (https://console.groq.com) — needed for the chat agent only

## LLM setup (once)
Store the key in .NET user-secrets (kept in your user profile, **outside the repo**; loaded in Development):
```powershell
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Groq:ApiKey" "<your-groq-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
# Optional extra fallback provider (free key at https://aistudio.google.com):
dotnet user-secrets set "Llm:Providers:Gemini:ApiKey" "<your-gemini-key>" --project src/WeatherRisk.Api
```
Outside Development use environment variables instead, e.g. `Llm__Providers__Groq__ApiKey`.
Without any key the app still runs; only `/api/chat` returns 503.

## Running

### Command line
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/WeatherRisk.Api --launch-profile http
```
Then open:
| URL | What |
|---|---|
| **http://localhost:5050/** | **Chat UI** — ask questions by typing or by voice 🎤 (Chrome/Edge) |
| http://localhost:5050/?q=Why%20is%20the%20Dallas%20hub%27s%20risk%20high%3F | Deep link: asks the question on load |
| http://localhost:5050/swagger | Swagger UI — try every endpoint live |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/rankings?region=Midwest&hazard=Winter | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/compare?hubs=miami,houston&hazards=Hurricane&hazards=Flood | Miami vs Houston, hurricane and flood |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/denver/weather | Denver last full year: snow days, % of days, … |
| http://localhost:5050/api/hubs/dallas/risk | Dallas risk breakdown: drivers, contributions, evidence |
| http://localhost:5050/api/risk/model | How scores are computed |
| http://localhost:5050/openapi/v1.json | OpenAPI document |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/health | Health check |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/metrics | Request metrics (counts, failures, rate-limited, latency) |
| http://localhost:5050/api/system/schema | Database schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) |

### Ask the agent
In Swagger (`POST /api/chat`) or from PowerShell:
```powershell
$r = Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body '{"message":"Why is the Dallas hub''s weather disruption risk high?"}'
$r.answer; $r.findings; $r.toolCalls
# Follow-up in the same conversation:
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:5050/api/chat -Method Post -ContentType application/json `
      -Body (@{ message = "How does it compare with Houston?"; conversationId = $r.conversationId } | ConvertTo-Json)
```

### Database
SQLite, created and migrated automatically on first start at `src/WeatherRisk.Api/App_Data/weatherrisk.db`
(15 hubs seeded). No setup needed. To reset, stop the app and delete the `App_Data` folder.

### External data
On startup the app downloads 5 years of daily weather (Open-Meteo) and FEMA hazard baselines for all hubs in
the background (~1 minute the first time — Open-Meteo's free per-minute quota; then cached for 30 days).
Internet access is needed for that first fetch; afterwards the app works from the cache. Progress and outcome:
`/api/system/health` and `/api/system/metrics` → `dependencies`.

For schema changes (developers):
```powershell
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/WeatherRisk.Data --output-dir Persistence/Migrations
```

### Visual Studio 2026
Open `WeatherRisk.slnx`, set **WeatherRisk.Api** as the startup project, choose the **http** profile, press F5.
The browser opens the chat UI.

### Chat UI
![Chat UI](docs/images/chat-answer.png)
- Type a question or tap an example; **🎤** dictates (Chrome/Edge — the browser asks for microphone permission);
  **🔊** reads answers aloud; **New chat** starts a fresh conversation (follow-ups keep context until then).
- Each answer shows the numbers it cites with **✓ verified** against the deterministic tools, key factors,
  caveats, follow-up suggestions, and **How I got this** (tools called, model, timing).

| `RateLimiting:Chat` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` | 10 / 60 | Per-client limit for `/api/chat` |
| `RateLimiting:Global` | `PermitLimit` / `WindowSeconds` / `SegmentsPerWindow` | 120 / 60 / 6 | Per-client sliding window for `/api/*` (except `/api/system/*`) |
